items.title: Philippine Police Detain Hundreds Protesting Trump Visit
items.description: Click to expand Image Protesters attempt to march to the ASEAN Summit venue in Manila but are stopped by hundreds of police officers, November 17, 2026. © 2026 Lian Buan/Human Rights Watch Police in the Philippines arrested and detained at least 245 people protesting the visit of US President Donald Trump to Manila for the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) summit. Protests in Manila started on November 15 opposing the Philippine government’s plan to build a technology manufacturing hub in Capas, Tarlac province, under the US government’s “Pax Silica” initiative. The construction will displace hundreds of Indigenous people and small farmers from their homes and farmlands. An estimated 6,000 people joined the protests despite police efforts to contain demonstrations by banning them everywhere except in “freedom parks” – designated areas where rallies can be held without a permit. Yet police arrested 236 people on the outskirts of Metro Manila who were traveling from the Southern Tagalog region to the main protest site. Among those detained were 29 farmers including members of the Indigenous Mangyan tribe, 19 journalists, 9 environmental defenders, and 6 human rights workers. Ephraim Cortez of the National Union of Peoples’ Lawyers said 19 children were detained. “This is the largest mass arrest we’ve seen under [President] Marcos,” protest leader Renato Reyes told Human Rights Watch. “Our whole delegation was arrested and taken to a police camp where lawyers were not given immediate access.” Detainees are being held inside a police camp in a hall with poor ventilation, insufficient drinking water, and inadequate restroom facilities, according to activists and lawyers. The protesters have been detained for three days without charge. Lawyers representing them expressed concern that they could face criminal charges of illegal assembly, alarms and scandals, and disobedience to authority. Police detained without charge another nine protesters at the main protest site on November 15 for attempting to march to the ASEAN summit venue. News footage shows police officers slapping and kicking a protester on the ground. International human rights law protects the right to peaceful assembly. Law enforcement may not carry out indiscriminate mass arrests even if a protest violates local laws or becomes disorderly. Arrests need to be based on individualized grounds and comply with the requirements of legality, necessity, and proportionality. Police can arrest people responsible for specific unlawful conduct but not just for taking part in a protest. All those arbitrarily detained for exercising their basic rights should be immediately released.

items.title: UGEL tried to stop me from inspecting UG hostels – Rent Commissioner
items.description: Acting Rent Commissioner Frederick Opoku says the University of Ghana Enterprise Limited (UGEL) formally asked him not to inspect its hostel facilities through a letter written by the company’s lawyers. He said the letter was received ahead of his inspection of the university’s hostels on Tuesday, which culminated in a heated confrontation between him and one of the hostel managers. Speaking on Joy FM on Wednesday, November 18, Mr Opoku said UGEL, through its legal representatives, communicated its objection to his intended visit to the facilities. “In fact, before we went there yesterday [Tuesday], they (UGEL) brought some lawyers, I don’t know where they were coming from, and wrote a letter to me at the Rent Control that we shouldn’t step there,” he claimed. The disclosure follows a viral video in which the Acting Rent Commissioner was seen in a heated exchange with a hostel manager during an inspection on the University of Ghana campus. In the video, the manager is heard telling Mr Opoku that President John Dramani Mahama would not approve of his conduct. The Commissioner, visibly agitated, responded by accusing the manager of stealing money and challenging him to take the matter to court. The confrontation nearly escalated into a fisticuff. READ ALSO: VIDEO: Tension at UG hostel as Rent Commissioner clashes with manager The incident has generated public debate about the authority of the Rent Control Department to inspect hostel facilities and the responsibilities of property managers to comply with rent regulations. The incident comes as the Acting Rent Commissioner intensifies nationwide inspections as part of efforts to enforce rent regulations and address concerns over the conduct of landlords and property managers. items.title: Sondages en France : Mélenchon s'ancre au second tour, Lisnard gagne du terrain à droite
items.description: « Quel que soit le scenario, le leader insoumis se hisserait au second tour », analyse ce 18 novembre Le Figaro , relayant les resultats du dernier barometre Ifop-Fiducial realise avec LCI et Sud Radio. « Le quadruple pretendant gagne encore du terrain, oscillant entre 17 % et 19,5 % selon les hypotheses », peut-on lire, le quotidien dressant un parallele avec le score que Jean-Luc Melenchon avait realise en 2017 a l'issue de sa campagne. En 2022, celui-ci avait manque de peu – avec 21,95 % des suffrages - le second tour, a quelques centaines de milliers de voix d'une Marine Le Pen (23,15 %) vampirisee par eric Zemmour (7,07 %). Ce dernier, note Le Figaro , serait en recul de 0,5 a 1,5 point, credite de 3 a 3,5 % des intentions de vote. « Sa declaration de candidature la semaine derniere n'a produit aucun effet, si ce n'est peut-etre l'inverse », juge le quotidien. Quant au candidat de La France insoumise, il reste pour l'heure bien loin de celle qui domine tous les sondages : Marine Le Pen. La candidate du Rassemblement national (RN) demeure nettement en tete, avec 32 a 36 % des intentions de vote, soit une quinzaine de points devant Jean-Luc Melenchon. Le Figaro souligne que la deputee du Pas-de-Calais « marque le pas apres avoir atteint un pic fin octobre, dopee par l'onde de choc des violences du 17 octobre » durant lesquelles, notamment, 3 000 commerces avaient ete la cible de saccages et pillages. Entre les deux, plusieurs candidats de la droite et du centre entendent organiser une primaire. En l'occurrence, le president des Republicains (LR) Bruno Retailleau, l'ex-Premier ministre macroniste – venu du Parti socialiste –, Gabriel Attal, ainsi que le maire de Cannes, president de l'Association des maires de France, David Lisnard. Ce dernier, en hausse de 2 a 3,5 points, « signe la plus forte progression de l'enquete », releve Le Figaro . Lisnard viendrait meme disputer la troisieme place au classement des presidentiables a edouard Philippe, credite de 10 a 15 % des voix, qui a refuse de participer a la primaire de la droite et du centre, et qui – d'apres la meme source – aurait certes « enraye sa chute » dans les sondages, mais « sans pour autant retrouver d'elan ». Une progression du maire de Cannes, soulignee par d'autres enquetes d'opinion, dont le barometre Ipsos bva-CESI pour La Tribune Dimanche , publiee le 14 novembre. Selon l'institut, 20 % des Francais se declareraient satisfaits de voir David Lisnard acceder a l'elysee, contre 16 % en octobre, uniquement devance par Marine Le Pen et Jordan Bardella, respectivement a 36 % et 34 %.

IOM Yemen Dispatch Situation Overview September 2026
items.description: Country: Yemen Source: International Organization for Migration Please refer to the attached file. SITUATION OVERVIEW Yemen’s security and humanitarian situation worsened significantly throughout September, driven by the continued spread of ground fighting following August’s violent escalations. Ground hostilities expanded rapidly across southwestern fronts, with Ansar Allah (AA) forces intensifying offensives in Ta’iz and Lahj as they attempted to consolidate gains on the West Coast by securing the overlooking mountains. The fighting triggered a massive surge in displacement, forcing over 160,140 individuals to flee their homes, particularly from the Maqbanah, Jabal Habashi, and Al Ma’afer districts in Ta’iz. Vital supply lines, including the crucial road linking Mokha to Ta’iz City, were severely disrupted and cut off, stranding communities and impacting humanitarian access. The AA forces claimed to have targeted several sites in Riyadh and the Aramco facilities in Yanbu, a Saudi Red Sea port, with missiles and drones. Saudi Arabia requested air defenses for critical facilities from Egypt, France, Pakistan, and the UK. French President Emmanuel Macron said France would send military assets to help protect Yanbu following the attack, as the concerns over maritime security and global oil prices grew. Saudi Arabia also reportedly urged the Government of Yemen (GoY) to call for a general mobilization, which was announced in a speech marking the anniversary of the September 26 Revolution. On the other side, in a move to capitalize on its capture of the Bab al-Mandeb and the West Coast, the AA-affiliated Red Sea Ports and Tax Customs Authorities announced reductions in vessel and container fees and port taxes, effective 1 October. The sharp escalation in violence severely strained Yemen’s already compromised health infrastructure, with hospitals in Ta’iz, Ma’rib, and Hadramaut overwhelmed by casualties. Major health centers were forced to suspend non-emergency care—such as maternity and obstetrics services—to reallocate scarce beds and medical personnel toward trauma management. The cholera epidemic maintained a strong hold across southern and western governorates, with transmission exacerbated by population displacement and damaged water and sanitation infrastructure. Abyan and Lahj continued to report the highest concentration of suspected cases, while newly displaced clusters in Ta’iz and Aden saw rising incidence rates. According to the IPC, nearly five million people faced crisis levels of hunger or worse in government-controlled areas between March and May, including 1.4 million in emergency conditions, and it has been observed that food security has significantly deteriorated since the escalation began. Wheat flour prices increased by 10 per cent in parts of Ta’iz as of late September, while traders estimate wheat stocks will cover only about two months of demand. At the UN General Assembly, 80 countries supported a statement condemning “the Houthis’ decision to resume the conflict in Yemen, their continuous strikes on Saudi Arabia, and their reckless attacks on the Red Sea.” UN Special Envoy Hans Grundberg met with AA negotiators in Muscat to avoid further escalation and held talks in Cairo with the regional powers, including Egypt and the League of Arab States.

items.title: Former Spain midfielder Mata retires aged 38
items.description: Former Spain midfielder Juan Mata has announced his retirement from playing at the age of 38. Mata, who made 41 international appearances, was part of the Spain squad that won the 2010 World Cup, and he helped his country win the European Championship two years later when he scored in the 4-0 final victory against Italy. A former Real Madrid youth player, he joined Valencia in 2007 before a move to Chelsea in August 2011 where he won the Champions League, Europa League and FA Cup. Mata moved to Manchester United in January 2014 and helped them claim the Europa League, FA Cup and League Cup prior to his departure in 2022. He went on to have spells at Turkish side Galatasaray and Vissel Kobe in Japan before he played for Australian sides Western Sydney Wanderers and Melbourne Victory. “Football will never leave my life,” said Mata. “There are so many ways to continue loving the game, so many ways to keep using it as a vehicle for development. “I may stop playing professionally, but I will never stop being a footballer.”

items.title: Man arrested for allegedly impersonating a prison officer in Tamale
items.description: A man claiming to be 19 years old has been arrested at Gumbihini, a suburb of Tamale, for allegedly impersonating a Ghana Prisons Service officer. The suspect, identified as Mohammed Yussif Zanjina, was arrested on Tuesday, November 17, at about 9:50 a.m. for allegedly wearing the Prisons Service’s No. 4 camouflage uniform without authorisation. According to a statement published by the Ghana Prisons Service on Facebook, the arrest was carried out by a Rapid Response Team led by Chief Officer Ahmed Mashood. The operation followed intelligence provided by Lance Corporal Haruna Mohammed Sherif. The suspect was subsequently presented to the Acting Second-in-Command of Tamale Central Prison, CSP Benedict Sanziri, for further interrogation. He was later handed over to the Regional Police Crime Officer for further investigations. CSP Sanziri commended L/Cpl Haruna Mohammed Sherif for providing the intelligence that led to the arrest and praised the Rapid Response Team for its swift response. The circumstances surrounding the alleged impersonation and the suspect’s motive were not immediately disclosed.

items.title: La protection civile de Ségou se dote d’un nouveau camion-citerne
items.description: La direction regionale de la protection civile de Segou dispose desormais d'un nouveau camion-citerne. Remis ce 1er novembre, ce vehicule d'une capacite de 6 000 litres est equipe de materiels specialises pour renforcer les interventions des equipes sur le terrain. Selon le directeur regional de la protection civile, cet appui vise a ameliorer les conditions de travail et l'efficacite operationnelle des agents. Le vehicule servira notamment a lutter contre les incendies, a porter secours aux victimes d'accidents de la circulation et a intervenir lors des cas de noyade. L’article La protection civile de Ségou se dote d’un nouveau camion-citerne est apparu en premier sur Studio Tamani - Informations, débats, magazines : toute l’actualité du Mali, en 5 langues .

items.title: Diplomatie | AES : Ouagadougou accueille le premier forum des ambassadeurs à la retraite
items.description: L'Association des ambassadeurs du Burkina Faso (ABF) à la retraite tient ce mercredi 18 novembre 2026 à Ouagadougou, le premier Forum des diplomates à la retraite de la confédération des l'Alliance des États du Sahel. Placé sous le thème général : « Expérience et expertise des diplomates à la retraite au service de la sécurité et du développement dans l'espace confédéral AES », la cérémonie d'ouverture a été présidée par le ministre des affaires étrangères du Burkina Faso, Karamoko Jean Marie Traoré, représentant du Premier ministre, patron. C'était en présence du président de la Commission nationale de la confédération de l'AES, Bassolma Bazié et d'autres membres du gouvernement. Dans le cadre du renforcement de la coopération entre les États membres de la Confédération des États du Sahel (AFS), les associations des diplomates à la retraite du Burkina Faso, du Mali et du Niger envisagent l'organisation d'un premier forum à Ouagadougou. Une vue des participants Cette rencontre vise à mettre à profit l'expérience et l'expertise des diplomates à la retraite afin de contribuer à la consolidation de l'intégration confédérale, au rayonnement international de l'AES et à la promotion d'une diplomatie concertée au service des peuples de l'espace sahélien. Il portera sur le thème général. Au-delà du thème général, les initiateurs tiendront des communications articulées autour des trois principaux piliers de la Confédération, à savoir: Défense, Diplomatie et Développement. Plus de détails à venir sur Minute.bf

items.title: La personnalité du président Kais Saïed, d’après l’IA
items.description: Dans cet article, l’auteur demande à trois algorithmes d’IA parmi les plus avancés (Gemini développé par Google, Claude par Anthropic et ChatGPT par Open.Ai) de décortiquer les discours du président Kais Saïed depuis qu’il est au pouvoir en vue de d’identifier les principaux traits de sa personnalité. S’agissant d’un personnage public dont tous les Tunisien(ne)s connaissent le discours et le bilan, il laisse à chacun(e) le soin d’estimer dans quelle mesure les trois IA ont réussi leur mission. Sadok Zerelli * Il est un fait que le développement et la mise à la disposition de tous gratuitement de modèles d’IA de plus en plus puissants et performants a bouleversé nos modes de pensée et d’apprentissage et constituent à ce titre un instrument d’analyse et d’investigation dont on ne peut plus de se passer. Parmi les sujets sur lesquels j’ai voulu tester l’intelligence indiscutable de ces modèles d’IA (voir mon article : L’IA est-elle intelligente ? ), figure leurs capacités à établir le portrait psychologique d’un être humain et identifier les principaux traits de sa personnalité, à partir de ses écrits ou de ses discours publics. C’est un exercice qui n’est pas évident à réussir car nos pensées, comportements et actions sont souvent influencées par notre intelligence et connaissances certes, mais aussi par nos frustrations et contradictions qui datent quelquefois de notre enfance et qui sont enfouies dans notre subconscient. Pour réussir ce test et être capable de juger la vraisemblance et la pertinence des réponses des modèles d’IA, il me fallait choisir un personnage public dont on connait tous les discours et sur lequel nous avons déjà une opinion sur sa personnalité, à savoir notre président Kais Saïed. Ma question était simple et exactement la même pour les trois IA les plus avancées que j’ai sélectionnées (Gemini, Claude et ChatGPT) : « Quels sont, selon toi, les principaux traits de la personnalité du président Kais Saïed, d’après ses discours politiques ». Comme à mon habitude dans ce genre d’exercice, je vais reproduire d’abord la réponse intégrale de chaque IA afin de satisfaire la curiosité des lecteurs et lectrices, avant d’apprécier les réponses et faire quelques remarques sur les performances des différentes IA questionnées. Les chances de Kaïs Saïed de gagner les présidentielles de 2029, selon trois IA La réponse de Gemini : A travers ses discours publics — de ses interventions télévisées à ses prises de parole improvisées —, le président tunisien Kaïs Saïed déploie un style rhétorique très singulier. Les politologues, sociologues et analystes du discours qui ont étudié ses allocutions dégagent plusieurs traits majeurs qui dessinent sa posture politique et sa manière d’exercer le pouvoir : 1. une posture de professeur de droit et d’exégète : avant d’être président, Kaïs Saïed est un universitaire spécialiste de droit constitutionnel, et cela transparaît constamment dans sa parole. Il adopte fréquemment le ton d’un enseignant qui explique, corrige ou rappelle les principes fondamentaux : – usage d’un arabe littéraire soutenu ( fusha ) ponctué de digressions grammaticales, étymologiques ou historiques, qui vise à projeter une image d’érudition et de supériorité intellectuelle ; – appel constant aux textes et aux principes (la Constitution, la légitimité révolutionnaire, la souveraineté), souvent interprétés de manière littérale ou personnalisée pour justifier ses décisions ; 2. un messianisme moral et un sens de la mission : dans de nombreuses allocutions, Saïed se met en scène comme un homme investi d’un devoir quasi sacré de «redressement» et de «purification» de la vie publique : – responsabilité devant Dieu, le peuple et l’Histoire : il invoque régulièrement le jugement divin et historique pour légitimer son action, se présentant comme un rempart solitaire face aux dérives du pays ; – moralisation de la politique : les crises économiques, sociales ou institutionnelles sont fréquemment ramenées à des questions d’éthique individuelle, de loyauté ou de trahison plutôt qu’à des arbitrages techniques ou partisans ; 3. une approche anti-institutionnelle et anti-partisane : sa rhétorique repose sur une défiance marquée envers les intermédiaires politiques classiques (partis, syndicats, parlements) : – relation directe au «peuple» : il oppose la volonté supposée pure et indivisible du peuple aux manœuvres des «clans» ou des «parties» intermédiaires ; – rejet du compromis partisan : la négociation politique est souvent disqualifiée au profit d’une logique binaire entre ceux qui servent l’intérêt général et ceux qui l’entravent ; 4. un penchant pour l’allusion et le récit complotiste : ses discours se caractérisent rarement par des bilans chiffrés ou des feuilles de route détaillées ; ils privilégient un registre allusif : – ennemis flous ou métaphoriques : il évoque régulièrement des «complots» , des «chambres obscures» ou des forces hostiles sans toujours nommer précisément les acteurs visés ; – métaphores vives et dévalorisantes : pour discréditer ses adversaires ou critiques, il recourt parfois à l’ironie mordante, au sarcasme ou à des images animalières et guerrières. 5. une image d’austérité et d’incorruptibilité : sur le plan de la mise en scène, Saïed cultive la sobriété : costume sombre, peu d’ostentation matérielle, refus affiché des codes mondains de la politique traditionnelle. Ses discours insistent sur la probité personnelle, le désintéressement et le rejet de la corruption comme socle de sa légitimité. 6. nuances selon les lectures : – p our ses partisans, ces traits traduisent l’intégrité d’un homme «hors système» , franc, attaché à la souveraineté nationale et à la dignité des citoyens face à une classe politique jugée corrompue ou impuissante ; – pour ses critiques, cette même rhétorique nourrit une personnalisation extrême du pouvoir, une méfiance envers le pluralisme démocratique et une tendance à criminaliser ou disqualifier toute opposition. La réponse de Claude Je ne peux pas faire un portrait psychologique d’un dirigeant à distance. Je peux en revanche relever les traits qui ressortent de ses discours selon les analystes, avec des lectures différentes selon les camps : – un moralisme de «mission» : AFP le décrit comme un homme qui se voit investi d’une mission divine, alors que ses détracteurs y voient l’installation d’un nouveau régime autoritaire. Ses discours opposent souvent les «purs» aux «corrompus» ; – un registre populiste : même ses discours sur le prix du pain sont formulés au nom du peuple, face à une élite politique. Cette logique du «nous» contre «eux» est aussi relevée par d'autres analystes ; – une rhétorique de rupture avec la méfiance envers les partis : il affirme que les partis ont pollué la vie politique et que le parlement ne représente pas la volonté du peuple. Un analyste estime que sa position a évolué avec les événements plutôt que de suivre un plan préétabli : – un style très personnel : ancien professeur de droit constitutionnel, il adopte une posture rigide et professorale. Il peut pourtant passer au dialecte tunisien, à l’ironie et à la dérision. Il est aussi amateur de calligraphie et écrit souvent ses discours à la plume ; – un ton souvent combatif : des observateurs relèvent des métaphores de plus en plus dures contre ses opposants ; – lectures opposées : ses partisans voient en lui un homme intègre, indépendant, qui tient tête à des élites corrompues ; alors que ses critiques estiment que ses vidéos donnent peu d’indications sur la politique économique et contiennent une rhétorique virulente contre ses adversaires. Certains parlent aussi d’un faux intellectualisme et d’un discours simpliste. La réponse de ChatGPT À mon sens, pour comprendre la personnalité publique de Kaïs Saïed, il faut partir d'un élément essentiel : ses discours politiques sont aussi révélateurs de sa conception du pouvoir, de l'État et de la relation entre le dirigeant et le peuple. Je ferais toutefois une distinction entre sa personnalité intime, que nous ne connaissons pas, et la personnalité politique qu'il donne à voir à travers ses discours, ses interventions publiques et sa manière de communiquer. C'est cette seconde dimension que je vais examiner. Les principaux traits de sa personnalité politique : à partir de ses prises de parole, je distinguerais huit caractéristiques. 1. un homme profondément attaché à l’autorité : c’est probablement l’un des traits les plus visibles de son expression politique. Il privilégie les notions d’autorité de l’État, de discipline, de respect de la loi et de restauration de l’ordre. Dans ses discours, le pouvoir apparaît souvent comme une autorité qui doit s’imposer plutôt que comme une institution qui doit négocier, composer et rechercher des compromis. Cela traduit une conception verticale de l’exercice du pouvoir; 2. un discours fortement moralisateur : Kaïs Saïed utilise fréquemment un vocabulaire moral : honnêteté, corruption, trahison, patriotisme, justice et probité. Il présente volontiers les problèmes politiques comme une opposition entre ceux qui servent l’intérêt général et ceux qui servent leurs intérêts particuliers. Cette rhétorique donne à ses interventions une dimension presque morale, parfois proche du jugement. Une étude linguistique publiée en 2025 relève notamment l’utilisation d’un ton professoral, la mobilisation des émotions et la construction d’une opposition entre le peuple et ses adversaires; 3. une conception personnalisée de la relation avec le peuple : son slogan de campagne de 2019, «Le peuple veut» , est particulièrement révélateur. Il privilégie une relation directe entre le président et le peuple, en contournant les partis politiques et les corps intermédiaires. Cette conception repose sur une idée : le président serait le représentant direct de la volonté populaire. Mais elle soulève une question fondamentale : comment distinguer la volonté réelle d’un peuple, qui est nécessairement pluriel, de celle que son dirigeant lui attribue ?; 4. un juridisme prononcé : sa formation de professeur de droit constitutionnel se retrouve dans sa manière de s’exprimer. Il aime les raisonnements juridiques, les références aux textes, les définitions et les formulations précises. Il parle souvent comme un enseignant qui expose une règle à ses étudiants. Cette caractéristique peut être appréciée comme une volonté de rigueur institutionnelle. Elle peut aussi donner à ses discours un caractère professoral et parfois difficilement accessible; 5. une méfiance marquée envers les élites et les intermédiaires : ses discours manifestent une défiance récurrente envers les partis, les parlementaires et certaines catégories de responsables politiques. Il oppose fréquemment les intérêts du peuple à ceux des élites politiques et économiques. Cette posture s’inscrit dans une rhétorique populiste au sens politique du terme : elle construit une opposition entre un peuple présenté comme légitime et des élites présentées comme responsables des dysfonctionnements; 6. un attachement à une certaine tradition conservatrice : ses discours font régulièrement référence à l’identité nationale, à l’histoire, à la culture arabo-musulmane et aux valeurs collectives. Il ne développe pas une vision libérale de la société au sens occidental du terme. Son approche met davantage l’accent sur la communauté, la souveraineté nationale, les traditions et l’autorité de l’État. Une recherche universitaire consacrée à cinq de ses discours présidentiels souligne précisément l’importance de ces références identitaires; 7. une communication solennelle et peu familière : son expression est caractérisée par : un arabe littéraire soutenu ; une diction particulièrement articulée ; des phrases souvent longues ; un ton professoral ; des références historiques, juridiques et religieuses. Il ne recherche pas nécessairement la proximité émotionnelle habituelle dans la communication politique. Il privilégie une posture de gravité et de solennité; 8. Une vision très centralisée de l’exercice du pouvoir : c’est ici que l’analyse de ses discours doit être confrontée à ses actes institutionnels. Depuis le 25 juillet 2021, la concentration des pouvoirs autour de la présidence et la réduction du rôle des contre-pouvoirs ont profondément transformé le système politique tunisien. La Constitution de 2022 a également renforcé la prééminence présidentielle. Il existe donc une continuité observable entre sa conception verticale de l’autorité et l’évolution institutionnelle du pays. Une dernière réflexion, plus philosophique : il y a une question qui me paraît particulièrement intéressante dans le cas de Kaïs Saïed : un dirigeant peut-il prétendre incarner la volonté du peuple sans accepter pleinement que ce peuple puisse avoir des opinions différentes des siennes ? C’est toute la difficulté de sa conception de la démocratie. La démocratie ne consiste pas seulement à donner la parole au peuple ou à invoquer sa souveraineté. Elle suppose également d’accepter la pluralité des opinions, la contradiction, le désaccord et l’existence de contre-pouvoirs. Et c’est précisément sur cette question que les discours de Kaïs Saïed et l’évolution des institutions tunisiennes méritent d’être examinés ensemble. Pour approfondir cette analyse, deux travaux sont particulièrement intéressants : l’étude de Jamil Ghouaidia sur sa rhétorique politique (2025) et celle de Kamilia Rahmouni sur le langage, le pouvoir et l’identité nationale (2023). Selon l’IA, y aura-t-il une nouvelle révolution en Tunisie ? Mon appréciation des réponses des IA Nous connaissons tous les discours de notre président et avons tous une opinion sur sa personnalité, sa capacité de communication et son bilan depuis qu’il est au pouvoir. Je laisserai donc à chaque lecteur et lectrices le soin d’estimer dans quelle mesure les réponses des différents IA sont pertinentes, objectives et réalistes. Pour ma part, je ferais trois observations relatives aux performances des trois algorithmes d’IA : a- les analyses des trois IA sont convergentes dans le sens où on retrouve les mêmes idées exprimées avec des mots et des phrases différents : ton professoral, un juridisme extrême, centralisation du pouvoir, opposition entre le peuple «victime» et les élites «corrompues», etc. ; b- en termes de pertinence d’analyse, d’argumentation et de clarté de rédaction, je classerai en premier ChatGPT (version 6 qui vient d’être mise sur le marché le 13 septembre 2026 par Open.AI) suivi par Gemini de Google et en dernier lieu par Claude d’Anthropic. C’est un classement qui va surprendre les partisans de Claude qui ne jurent que par cet algorithme qu’ils considèrent comme le meilleur : il l’est peut-être pour des tâches de codage, ou de piratage ou de traitement de très gros fichiers, mais à mon avis et selon mon expérience, pas en tant qu’agent conversationnel ; c- si l’IA est capable d’élaborer le portrait psychologique et d’identifier les qualités et défauts d’un être humain à partir de l’analyse de ses seuls discours ou de ses écrits, comme ce test semble le montrer, elle pourrait apprendre aussi certains défauts des humains tels que mentir, être autoritaire, hypocrite, voire méchant ou même diabolique. Sachant que des experts en IA parmi les plus imminents, tels que Bill Gates ou Jacob Coxon (ce jeune britannique, expert en IA qui vient de démissionner en septembre 2026 d’Anthropic parce que sa conscience ne lui permettait pas de contribuer au développement d’un outil dont il est convaincu qu’il finira par détruire toute l’humanité) estiment que, si le développement des IA continue à cette vitesse, la probabilité que l’IA tuera d’une manière ou d’une autre tous les êtres humains sur terre dans un horizon de dix ans, est de 20%, voire même 50% pour certains, cette capacité à comprendre la psychologie humaine est plutôt une mauvaise nouvelle pour le sort de l’humanité à moyen et long terme. * Economiste universitaire et consultant international. L’article La personnalité du président Kais Saïed, d’après l’IA est apparu en premier sur Kapitalis .

items.title: Drone strikes in Sudan leave children with nowhere to escape as conflict worsens
items.description: Country: Sudan Source: World Vision More than 800 civilians, including children, have been killed with nearly 100,000 in Blue Nile displaced This month 25 strikes have been recorded in 11 states, with hospitals, power stations, markets and homes all being targeted World Vision calls on all sides to stop killing children and let essential aid flow Drone strikes are killing hundreds of people in Sudan every month, leaving children and families facing hunger, a lack of clean water, and increased security risks as the number of drone strikes continues to escalate, says World Vision, which is calling on all sides to stop targeting civilians. At least 880 civilians have been killed between January and May 2026, accounting for approximately 80 per cent of all civilian deaths. Civilians are being killed in markets, hospitals, displacement camps, and transport hubs. TJ Grant, National Director, World Vision New Zealand , says, "Children and civilians are not collateral damage. Even if they aren’t targeted directly, they are the ones that suffer the consequences when essential services are targeted." "Without power clean water cannot be pumped, hospitals can’t function, and health centres can’t keep medicines and vaccines safe. Parents risk their lives every time they go to the market to buy food. Aid agencies are also facing tough choices, often forced to cancel aid trips due to drone activity, leaving thousands without the vital support they desperately need." Last month alone, more than 300 people in Sudan were killed, most of them civilians. At least 25 strikes have been recorded across 11 states so far this month, including areas far from active frontlines. In Damazin, the Blue Nile State capital, drone strikes hit the Rosieres Dam Transmission Station and the city’s power plant, cutting electricity. The situation is worsening, according to the latest figures from the Sudan INGO Forum, of which World Vision is a member. Attacks on infrastructure are impacting power supplies, health care provisions, and people’s ability to buy food and fuel. In one day alone, drones struck six power stations, disrupting electricity across south-east Sudan. Simon Mane, National Director for World Vision Sudan , says: "This must stop. Children and civilians have already fled fighting. Now the drones are following them, leaving them with no place to run." Mass casualty incidents are also increasing. A 26 October attack on a market in Nyala, South Darfur, killed or injured more than 150 people, while a drone strike near Amiet Market and Todach in the Abyei area on 19 October left dozens more civilians dead or injured. Mane says, "Drones are targeting the power, fuel, and water supplies people depend on to survive. When a power station is hit, the consequences reach far beyond the site itself, affecting a child on oxygen in hospital, a patient needing dialysis, and families are left without access to clean water." Security conditions in Blue Nile continue to deteriorate, with nearly 100,000 people displaced and growing fears of hunger as El Niño threatens the critical harvest season. World Vision Sudan staff are providing life-saving assistance to hundreds of thousands of children and families on both sides of the conflict. However, movement restrictions, fuel shortages, and rising costs are making it difficult to reach those in need. World Vision calls for all sides to: Stop targeting civilians and essential infrastructure (power, fuel and water systems) Protect displacement sites from fighting Permit humanitarian access and support for displaced and host communities affected by ongoing violence Allow civilians to access farms, grazing lands, and agricultural and market infrastructure during this critical harvest period to prevent widespread hunger -ENDS- For more information contact: Ashley Miln | Media and PR Advisor, World Vision Email: ashley.miln@worldvision.org.nz +64-204-051-3769

items.title: We do not fall under the Rent Act; hostel occupants are not tenants – UGEL Chief Officer
items.description: The Chief Executive Officer of the University of Ghana Enterprise Limited (UGEL), Yawo Agbesi, has argued that the university’s hostel facilities do not fall under the Rent Act of the Rent Control Commission of the Ministry of Works, Housing and Water Resources because students who occupy them are not tenants. He explained that UGEL does not enter into conventional landlord-tenant agreements with students, who instead apply for accommodation and leave the facilities after completing their studies. According to him, the students are considered constituents of the university’s accommodation system rather than tenants under a landlord-tenant arrangement. “We are of the view that our students, or our constituents, as we call them, are not tenants and, among other things, we do not fall under the Rent Act, and it is subject to some level of interpretation,” he said on JoyFM’s Super Morning Show on Wednesday. “We are not disputing the power and authority of the Rent Commissioner; he is doing a fantastic job, and we respect him for what he is doing, but we are of the view that, from the way we operate, we are not operating from a landlord-tenant relationship,” he added. Mr Agbesi emphasised that “They [students] come in, they pay for a short period, they leave, and then the next semester they apply.” Mr Agbesi’s comments follow a confrontation between Acting Rent Commissioner Frederick Opoku and a hostel manager during an inspection of UGEL-operated facilities on the University of Ghana campus. Read Also: Acting Rent Commissioner explains why no arrests were made during UG Hostel visit despite clashes with manager The incident, which was captured in a viral video, has triggered debate over the authority of the Rent Control Department to inspect the university’s hostels. Mr Opoku has disclosed that UGEL, through its lawyers, wrote to him asking him not to visit the facilities. UGEL says it is preparing to file a court action to seek interpretation of the Rent Act in relation to hostels.

items.title: Classement FIFA : le Sénégal reste 18e mondial, 2e africain
items.description: Le classement FIFA du mois de novembre 2026 a été dévoilé. Le Sénégal reste 18e au plan mondial. Côté africain, la sélection entrainée par Patrick Vieira est 2e, derrière le Maroc. Le Sénégal conserve le rang qu'il occupait depuis la mise à jour du 7 octobre. Les hommes de Patrick Vieira ont pourtant réussi leur fenêtre internationale, avec deux succès contre le Soudan (4-1 et 4-2) et une qualification pour la CAN 2027 désormais officielle. Cela n'a pas suffi à leur faire gagner un rang, mais ils restent dans le top 20 mondial, devant plusieurs nations de renom. Le Maroc au sommet de l'histoire africaine Les Lions de l'Atlas sont la grande révélation de ce classement. En passant au 5e rang, ils égalent la meilleure position jamais atteinte par une équipe africaine, celle du Nigeria en avril 1994. En tête, l'Espagne reste numéro un malgré sa défaite 3-2 contre l'Angleterre le 15 novembre. Elle devance l'Argentine et la France. Les Anglais complètent le top 4. items.title: Cyberattaque mondiale : 178 organisations ciblées pour voler des cryptomonnaies et piéger des iPhone
items.description: Des sites de grandes entreprises et de medias, parmi lesquels Zoom, HSBC, IKEA, CNN et Air France-KLM, ont diffuse a leur insu un code malveillant le 16 novembre. Selon le chercheur Scott Helme, de Report URI, les visiteurs de 178 organisations ont ete exposes a une attaque destinee a detourner des transferts en cryptomonnaies, recuperer des donnees bancaires et exploiter des failles d'iPhone. Les pirates n'ont pas eu besoin de penetrer les systemes de chaque entreprise. Ils ont exploite une vulnerabilite d'Optimizely, un service utilise pour tester et personnaliser les pages web. En modifiant un programme charge automatiquement par les sites clients, ils ont pu propager leur logiciel malveillant a grande echelle. Les chercheurs ont recense 188 scripts infectes. Les dessous dangereux de l'IA L'outil pouvait remplacer l'adresse d'un portefeuille numerique par celle des attaquants au moment d'un paiement. Il cherchait aussi a intercepter les numeros de carte saisis sur les pages concernees et a collecter certaines donnees de navigation. Sur iPhone et iPad, il tentait de declencher des logiciels tirant parti de failles d'anciennes versions d'iOS. Rien ne permet toutefois d'affirmer que tous les visiteurs ont ete infectes. Report URI a repere des transferts de cryptomonnaies detournes, pour quelque 7 000 dollars au 17 novembre. L'ampleur des eventuels vols de donnees bancaires reste inconnue. Optimizely a reconnu la faille, indique l'avoir corrigee le 16 novembre et retire les scripts compromis. Apple assure que les vulnerabilites visees avaient deja ete corrigees dans les versions a jour de son systeme. L'affaire illustre le risque des attaques dites « par la chaîne d'approvisionnement » : compromettre un prestataire suffit a atteindre des dizaines de marques. a l'ere de l'intelligence artificielle (IA), qui permet aussi d'automatiser certaines operations malveillantes, la menace gagne en vitesse et en envergure. Aucun usage de l'IA n'a cependant ete etabli dans l'attaque en question.

items.title: World: MSF calls for stronger AMR response to protect people affected by conflict
items.description: Country: World Source: Médecins Sans Frontières Rome, 18 Nov 26 - As the world marks World Antimicrobial Resistance (AMR) Awareness Week, MSF called on governments and funders to recognize the enormous toll that antimicrobial resistance is taking in conflict-affected and humanitarian contexts and act urgently by better equipping communities to prevent, detect, and respond to drug-resistant infections - before, during, and after times of acute crisis. Over two billion people are estimated to live in conflict-affected settings, and, in 2025, forced displacement affected an unprecedented 122 million people. In specific, at the Fourth Plenary Assembly of the AMR Multi-Stakeholder Partnership Platform held in Rome, Italy this week, MSF asked governments and funders to: • Invest before crises to fund national AMR plans that strengthen infection prevention and control (IPC), water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH), stewardship and laboratories • Plan for crises along with affected communities to build AMR into emergency preparedness and adapt national AMR plans in protracted crises, implementing context-specific interventions • Protect health care to uphold international humanitarian law • Count everyone to include conflict settings in surveillance and research, and ensure equitable access to antimicrobials and diagnostics “For the people we treat, antimicrobial resistance is not a 2050 projection. It is a newborn with sepsis, or a person with a war wound, whose infection no longer responds to the antibiotics we have,” said Dr Cecilia Ferreyra, infectious diseases specialist and Deputy to the International Medical Secretary of MSF. “The global fight against antimicrobial resistance will fail if it leaves behind people who are living through conflict and displacement. We are asking governments and donors for dedicated funding and adapted national AMR plans that include people vulnerable to crises from the start. The commitments made here and in the Ministerial Conference in Abuja next month will help decide whether these patients still have medical tools that work.” The risks and consequences of AMR are especially acute in settings affected by conflict and humanitarian crises, where inadequate WASH measures, poor infection prevention and control, and limited access to microbiology, diagnostic capacity, and appropriate antimicrobials contribute to emergence and spread of drug-resistant infections. Destruction of healthcare facilities and infrastructure for water and sanitation, shortages of healthcare workers, disrupted supply chains, and overcrowded living conditions further compound the AMR crisis. ​ MSF addresses AMR in more than 20 countries through over 50 projects, focusing on infection prevention and control, antibiotic stewardship, microbiology-based diagnostics, and surveillance. Our teams see the diversity of ways in which crises subject people to risk for and from AMR. From treating patients with severe wounds and drug-resistant infections to caring for malnourished children and newborns with sepsis, and people living with HIV who develop opportunistic infections, MSF works to strengthen healthcare workers’ capacity to counter AMR through provision of quality, people-centered care. “Antimicrobial resistance is increasingly becoming a consequence of conflict, displacement and fragile health systems,” said Dr Rupa Kanapathipillai, Antimicrobial Stewardship Lead, MSF Operational Centre Paris. “In Gaza, facilities designed for 250–300 patients a day received as many as 700, with wound care provided from shared trolleys. In South Sudan, Ethiopia and Nigeria, where displacement, flooding and outbreaks hit already stretched clinics, premature babies with sepsis and severely malnourished children are being treated where our antibiograms show high resistance, even in remote areas. Resistance follows displacement and weak health systems, not just the front line.” Global initiatives, including the updated Global Action Plan on AMR (adopted in May 2026), the planned launch of the Independent Panel for Evidence for Action against AMR, at the 5th Global High-Level Ministerial Conference on AMR in Abuja, Nigeria (6–8 December 2026), offer important opportunities to accelerate action. These initiatives are particularly crucial in light of recent shocks to global health and humanitarian financing that are taking us backwards rather than ahead. ​ “At the upcoming Ministerial Conference in Nigeria, governments must make concrete commitments and ensure that the Independent Panel on Evidence for Action against AMR will close critical evidence gaps in conflict-affected and humanitarian settings and translating evidence into action,” said Pauline Londeix, Advocacy Advisor, MSF Access. “Meaningful representation of humanitarian actors, affected communities and low-income countries is also essential to guarantee the Panel’s work responds to the needs of people most at risk.” For interviews, please contact: Mildred Wanyonyi: +254720260618 / mildred.wanyonyi@nairobi.msf.org

items.title: Le Niger à Abidjan : Hamadou Tini au cœur des grands choix énergétiques de l’Afrique…
items.description: Le ministre nigérien du Pétrole, Hamadou Tini, prend part depuis le mardi 17 novembre 2026 à Abidjan, à la 50e session ordinaire du Conseil ministériel de l’Organisation des producteurs de pétrole africains (APPO). Cette rencontre est importante, à un moment où l’Afrique cherche à mieux maîtriser ses ressources pétrolières et gazières, à financer ses infrastructures et à renforcer son indépendance énergétique. Sous la présidence du ministre ivoirien des Mines, du Pétrole et de l’Énergie, Mamadou Sangafowa-Coulibaly, les délégations venues de plusieurs pays du continent ont examiné les grandes orientations de l’organisation. Les discussions ont notamment porté sur le rapport d’activité de l’APPO, les recommandations du Conseil exécutif, le contenu local, le transfert de technologies, le raffinage ainsi que le développement des infrastructures gazières régionales. Pour le Niger, la participation de Hamadou Tini à cette rencontre revêt un enjeu particulier. Elle offre au pays une tribune pour défendre ses intérêts dans un espace où se construisent les priorités de la coopération énergétique africaine. Il s’agit notamment de valoriser davantage les ressources sur place, de renforcer les capacités industrielles nationales et d’attirer les financements nécessaires aux projets structurants. Le Niger entend ainsi faire entendre sa voix dans les débats sur l’avenir énergétique du continent. Les ministres ont aussi souligné la nécessité de mieux coordonner les stratégies nationales afin d’optimiser la valorisation des hydrocarbures africains. L’ambition est de transformer davantage les ressources sur le continent, de créer de la valeur localement et de réduire la dépendance des États africains aux financements extérieurs. Cette 50e session clôt une série de rencontres statutaires débutée le samedi 14 novembre 2026. Le Conseil exécutif de l’APPO s’est réuni les 15 et 16 novembre afin de préparer les dossiers soumis aux ministres, notamment le bilan de l’exercice 2026, le programme de travail, le budget prévisionnel 2027 et les réformes institutionnelles. Parmi les sujets majeurs figure l’opérationnalisation de la Banque africaine de l’énergie (BAE). Créée officiellement le 31 octobre 2026 à Abuja, en partenariat avec Afreximbank, elle devrait démarrer ses activités le 2 janvier 2027. Cette institution est présentée comme un levier essentiel pour financer les projets énergétiques africains et accompagner la réalisation des infrastructures stratégiques du continent. La délégation nigérienne, conduite par Hamadou Tini, restera à Abidjan pour participer, à partir de ce mercredi 18 novembre, au SIREXE 2026, le Salon international des ressources extractives et de l’énergie. Organisé jusqu’au 22 novembre au Parc des Expositions d’Abidjan, ce rendez-vous réunit gouvernements, entreprises, investisseurs, institutions financières et experts autour des défis liés aux mines, au pétrole, au gaz et à l’énergie. Cette deuxième édition a pour thème : « Industries extractives et énergétiques : quelles infrastructures pour soutenir le développement économique en Afrique ? » Pour le Niger, cette participation s’inscrit dans une dynamique plus large : faire entendre sa voix, saisir les opportunités de partenariats et contribuer à une Afrique capable de transformer ses richesses en développement réel pour ses populations. L’article Le Niger à Abidjan : Hamadou Tini au cœur des grands choix énergétiques de l’Afrique… est apparu en premier sur Tamtaminfo .

UGEL to seek court interpretation of Rent Act’s applicability to university hostels
items.description: The University of Ghana Enterprise Limited (UGEL) is preparing to take the Rent Control Commission to court to seek a judicial interpretation of the Rent Act and establish whether university-managed hostels fall within the scope of the legislation Chief Executive Officer of UGEL, Yawo Agbesi, said the move is intended to clarify whether the law applies to student accommodation facilities operated by universities. He argued that students occupying UGEL-managed hostels should not be regarded as conventional tenants, explaining that they apply for accommodation and vacate the facilities upon completing their studies, unlike tenants under traditional landlord-tenant arrangements. Mr Agbesi said UGEL wants the courts to interpret the relevant provisions of the Rent Act and determine whether they cover university-managed student accommodation. “We are in the process of seeking that interpretation,” he said when Winston Amoah asked, “Have you gone to court?” He added that the proposed legal action should not be interpreted as a confrontation with the Rent Control Commission. “If you say you are even going to court, it looks as if there is a direct conflict. There is no conflict situation, we are just saying that we just want to seek interpretation of the Rent Act and ask whether hostels fall under the Rent Act, so we are in the process of putting all that in motion.” The development follows a confrontation between Acting Rent Commissioner Frederick Opoku and a hostel manager during an inspection of UGEL facilities on the University of Ghana campus. The incident, which went viral on social media, sparked debate over the Rent Control Commission’s authority to inspect university hostels. Mr Opoku had earlier disclosed that UGEL, through its lawyers, had written to him asking him not to visit the facilities. However, speaking on Joy FM, the Acting Rent Commissioner said his office was ready to appear before the court to address the matter if the case was brought before it. “I don’t have much to say. They say they are going to court; we are waiting for them. Mr Agbesi is a lawyer, and Legon (University of Ghana) has lawyers; they can marshal all their lawyers and let us be in court,” he said. The planned legal action is expected to clarify the regulatory framework governing university hostels and determine whether such facilities are subject to the provisions of the Rent Act.

items.title: Bobo-Dioulasso : Les 72 Heures de la Presse Bobolaise annoncées du 26 au 28 novembre 2026
items.description: Les professionnels des médias de Bobo-Dioulasso organisent, du 26 au 28 novembre 2026, la première édition des 72 Heures de la Presse Bobolaise. Prévu à la Place de la Mairie centrale, cet événement ambitionne de renforcer les liens entre les acteurs des médias, les entreprises, les institutions et les populations. Les grandes articulations de cette manifestation ont été dévoilées à la presse, le samedi 14 novembre 2026, au cours d’une conférence de presse. Placée sous le thème « Médias et développement local : quelle synergie d’action pour promouvoir l’émergence des entreprises ? », la rencontre se veut un cadre de concertation et de rapprochement entre les professionnels de l’information et les autres acteurs du développement local. Durant trois jours, plusieurs activités meubleront cette manifestation. Au programme figurent notamment des panels consacrés aux enjeux du journalisme et aux relations entre les médias et les acteurs culturels. Une action de solidarité sera également organisée en mémoire des confrères disparus. À cela s’ajoutent un cross populaire réunissant des journalistes et des éléments des Forces de défense et de sécurité, ainsi qu’une plantation symbolique de l’arbre de la presse. Les échanges porteront également sur les questions de citoyenneté. Les organisateurs prévoient, par ailleurs, une reconnaissance du mérite des doyens de la presse bobolaise, en hommage à leur contribution au développement du paysage médiatique local. En marge de ces activités, un Plateau OFF offrira chaque soir un espace d’expression aux artistes et acteurs culturels de la région, à travers diverses prestations. À travers cette initiative, les promoteurs entendent faire des 72 Heures de la Presse Bobolaise un rendez-vous fédérateur. Au-delà de la promotion du métier de journaliste, ils ambitionnent de consolider la confraternité entre les professionnels des médias, de rapprocher davantage la presse des populations et de favoriser de nouvelles collaborations avec le secteur économique. items.title: In South Sudan, New Lifelines for Mothers and Babies
items.description: Country: South Sudan Source: Direct Relief In a region where pregnant women still face dangerous journeys to give birth, emergency transportation and medical supplies are helping transform maternal care. On September 21, a pregnant woman collapsed in a remote South Sudanese town, where reaching a hospital can mean hours of travel along roads that become nearly impassable in the rainy season. But for the first time, help came on three wheels. One of four newly launched motorcycle ambulances rushed the woman to Mother Teresa Hospital, marking a lifesaving first-day test of an emergency transport system designed to reach mothers in some of the country’s most isolated communities, including displacement camps. South Sudan has the world’s highest estimated neonatal mortality rate, with roughly one in 25 babies dying within their first 28 days of life, according to United Nations Inter-agency Group for Child Mortality Estimation data published last year . South Sudan also has one of the world’s highest maternal mortality rates, with an estimated 692 deaths per 100,000 live births in 2023 . Against that backdrop, local health workers report a striking development. “It has given us the good news up to now. We have no neonatal deaths and no deaths of the mother,” said Joseph Makuach, health coordinator for Transformation of the World in Christ, or TWIC , a local organization, which shares its acronym with the South Sudanese county of Twic, that coordinates medical services. Working alongside a network of community clinics and Mother Teresa Hospital, the ambulance, which was funded by Direct Relief partner MAMA Project , transports women in labor and patients experiencing obstetric emergencies to facilities equipped to provide care. Recent shipments of midwife kits from Direct Relief have added essential supplies needed for safer deliveries. Reaching Mothers Before It’s Too Late TWIC, the nonprofit, supports six primary health care clinics serving rural communities and internally displaced people. The clinics are located in Ayak Makot, Biemnhom, Bombil, Akotong, Madou, and Gogrial West. The new fleet of motorcycle ambulances, built in Uganda, helps connect these communities with Mother Teresa Hospital and other local healthcare facilities operated by international NGOs. The vehicles have proved unexpectedly effective in difficult terrain. Unlike heavier ambulances, the motorcycles can navigate narrow, damaged roads and can be pushed free when they become stuck in mud. When a woman needs emergency transport, community members contact TWIC staff, who coordinate with drivers and the receiving hospital. The vehicles have drivers and fuel available to respond. The Supplies Behind Safer Deliveries Transportation, however, is only part of the challenge. Mother Teresa Hospital, the principal referral hospital in Twic County, has long struggled with shortages of essential medical supplies and adequately compensated health workers. Direct Relief recently provided 15 midwife kits through TWIC’s partner network, with distributions to Mother Teresa Hospital, Lighthouse Hospital in Aweil, and nursing and midwifery partners associated with Juba Teaching Hospital. The donated supplies include sterile gauze, gloves, umbilical cord clamps, disinfectants, and medicines such as magnesium sulfate and misoprostol, used in managing complications of pregnancy and childbirth. Together, the materials help health workers maintain hygienic conditions and respond to emergencies. Dr. Luka Matik, director of Mother Teresa Hospital, said the supplies have improved conditions for mothers and newborns during both vaginal and cesarean deliveries. “Safety and hygiene, they ensure safety for the mothers and babies,” Matik said, explaining that clean delivery practices reduce the risk of infections. Matik said deliveries at the hospital have increased since the kits arrived, an indication, he believes, that women are gaining confidence in the care available. “If a mother comes and delivers and sees she’s well taken care of, she will go ahead and spread the word,” he said. In October, the hospital performed 20 cesarean sections, including procedures for women referred from surrounding health facilities. The impact of the donated supplies extends to Aweil, in neighboring Northern Bahr el Ghazal state. At Lighthouse Hospital and its outreach centers, health workers recorded 180 deliveries resulting in 182 newborns in October, according to a report submitted to Direct Relief. The facilities also provided antenatal care to 480 clients and referred five women to Aweil Civil Hospital for cesarean sections. No maternal deaths were recorded during the month. For Teresa Paul, a midwife at Lighthouse Hospital, the difference is apparent when women arrive in labor, particularly at night. “Before the kits arrived, we often struggled with shortages of gloves, plastic sheets, cord clamps and chlorhexidine,” she said in a statement included in the hospital’s report. “When a mother came into labor at night, and supplies were not available, it was heartbreaking.” “Now we can reassure mothers that essential delivery supplies are ready.” For some patients, the benefits are also financial. Mary Abuk Garang, a 32-year-old mother who received care at Lighthouse Hospital, said she arrived without the supplies needed for childbirth. “I came with nothing, but I received what I needed for my delivery,” she said in a testimonial provided by the hospital. Dr. Repent Khamis George, principal of the Juba College of Nursing and Midwives, said midwife kits were distributed to three primary health care centers around Juba, the nation’s capital, where staff welcomed supplies that are often difficult to obtain. Progress Amid Persistent Shortages Despite the reported improvements, formidable challenges remain. Matik said Mother Teresa Hospital needs additional surgical nurses, disinfectants, cleaning materials, intravenous fluids, catheters, and basic linens. Some health workers have gone months without government-funded incentive payments, placing additional pressure on colleagues supported by TWIC. Even as these personnel challenges and other stark issues remain, Makuach, TWIC’s health coordinator, assessed recent developments in lives saved. “Our situation is not like before,” he said. Since 2025, Direct Relief has provided $3.2 million in medical aid to support the health work of Transformation of the World in Christ in South Sudan.

items.title: 'He who claims equity must come with clean hands': Asif hits back at Bilawal
items.description: Defence Minister Khawaja Asif joined others from the ruling PML-N on Wednesday in responding to PPP Chairperson Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari following the latter’s hard-hitting speech over several issues, including new provinces, constitutional tweaks and treatment of the opposition. “He who claims equity must come with clean hands,” Asif reminded Bilawal in a post on X, as the wrangling between coalition partners PML-N and PPP appeared to deepen. The exchange has particularly heated up after Bilawal delivered a no-holds-barred speech the previous day that covered the question of new provinces. The Bhutto scion also expressed support for several opposition demands and questioned past decisions and actions taken by the ruling coalition. Bilawal referred to Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi’s recommendation of holding a referendum to decide on the creation of new administrative units and said: “In our history, a referendum has always been carried out for an undemocratic act and never a democratic one.” The PPP chairperson also remarked that the governance system had not collapsed, but was rather “made to collapse” — seemingly reacting to Naqvi’s statement in July that the current “system” of governance had “collapsed” and needed a “reset”. Asif began his response to Bilawal by addressing this matter. He said: “No system can reset without public support. If you are talking about a system collapse, then all of us, as people connected to this system, must also take stock of our responsibilities. The defence minister also appeared to throw his weight behind the proposal for holding a referendum on new provinces as he said that there would surely be a debate on “system reset” in Parliament, but the public too could not be “deprived of its fundamental right”. “The pinnacle of legitimacy would be reached if the public opinion is also taken into account along with that of Parliament.” Seemingly reacting to Bilawal’s support for the release of incarcerated former prime minister and PTI founder Imran Khan and other demands by the opposition, Asif added: “Holding politicians accountable in this country is nothing new, and no politician exempt from accountability.” He mentioned that the PPP had been in power in Sindh for 18 years. “Sindh has turned into paradise. The world admires the condition of Karachi,” he said, seemingly taking a jibe at the PPP, which is often criticised over the lack of development in Sindh. Asif then said Bilawal and his party had been a “partner of the PML-N in the business of government since 2022. You get the profit and the PML-N and Pakistan suffer loss”. “He who claims equity must come with clean hands,” Asif continued. “This is a centuries-old maxim of equity. Are your hands clean? Do you have the right to lecture or threaten?” The defence minister said, “We have just one objective: to change the lives of the people of Pakistan so that ordinary people can live with dignity. Make public participation in governance a reality … Do not confine the people’s rights to the pages of the Constitution.” He said after achievements on diplomatic and military fronts, now the “fight is for devolving governance to grassroots, in which public opinion and Parliament’s role are entirely democratic and constitutional. Governance is not anyone’s monopoly; Allah has granted this right to 250 million people.” ‘Sins are not washed away in this manner’ Minister of State for Interior Tallal Chaudhry also reacted to Bilawal’s speech, saying that while the Bhutto scion presented himself as a “champion” of the Constitution and democracy, he was well versed only in theory on the subject and, in practice, his performance was “zero”. He said Bilawal’s remarks the previous day were akin to picking and choosing certain provisions of the Constitution that suited him and disregarding others as unconstitutional. Chaudhry said the PPP was currently in power in three provinces, as well as Gilgit-Baltistan. The president and Senate chairperson were also from the PPP, he further pointed out, commenting: “And then you give the impression as if you are the opposition leader, as if you are not associated with the government in any way.” He also appeared to be criticising the PPP for being in favour of the creation of a south Punjab province and opposing the carving out of new administrative units in Sindh. “So you call for breaking an administrative unit where governance is good and those where governance is bad should be left?” The minister said Bilawal had also remarked that the 27th Amendment had been passed “with brute majority”. “Were the votes cast the same way for the 1973 Constitution, or the 18th Amendment? Or do you believe that after voting like this, you can hold a press conference, act innocent and dissociate yourself, [as if] you did not realise [what was happening]. “Then you may also vote for the legislation for administrative units and later hold such a press conference saying it was due to force. “Sins are not washed away in this manner. You cannot dissociate yourself in this manner,” he added. “Everyone remembers that speech of yours in the National Assembly in which you said that a constitutional court was Quaid-i-Azam’s dream,” Chaudhry recalled. “Then you referenced your mother’s speeches saying she wanted to create a constitutional court, and then you said — ‘This is our legacy. Carrying forward our legacy, today we have done the work that we had been wanting to do for the past 50 years’ — meaning the PPP wanted to do it. You took credit for the entire amendment, and today you’re saying that votes were cast forcibly.” Chaudhry claimed Bilawal and his party opposed creation of new provinces in order to maintain control over resources. He referred to the PPP chairperson’s statement that if Sindh were to be divided, there could be bloodshed and called it “regrettable”. “The question is: does casting a vote cause blood to flow, or does it stop bloodshed? You always say the decision should come through the ballot, not the bullet. So when did you start fearing the vote?” Chaudhry said. “During 17 years of [PPP] rule, your governance has drained the blood of the people of Sindh. First check whether any blood is even left in them or not,” Chaudhry quipped. According to the state minister, Bilawal merely wanted to accept “half the constitution” while claiming the rest as wrongly framed. “In other words, are you calling the very Constitution you framed unconstitutional?” he asked. “Democracy is not merely about delivering speeches, interpreting or explaining articles of the Constitution to show these are the rights of the people. Democracy also involves performance. Democracy also entails governance,” he added. In response to Bilawal’s remarks on the 27th Amendment, Chaudhry said such amendments to the Constitution had been made over time to improve governance and held that the 27 amendments so far had also been made with that objective. ‘PPP crushed the move’ Separately, Health Minister Mustafa Kamal, whose party had also been demanding the creation of new administrative units in the country, questioned why the PPP was worried over the creation of new provinces if its performance in the government had been good. Addressing a press conference in Islamabad, he painted a derelict picture of Sindh and asserted that power should be devolved to provinces. He said the Muttahida Qaumi Movement-Pakistan had tried to get this done through the 26th and 27th Constitutional Amendments, “but the PPP crushed” the move.

items.title: Shatta Wale says he feels bad seeing Majesty sell juice in the sun, tells Michy to prioritise his son’s welfare
items.description: Ghanaian dancehall artiste Shatta Wale has expressed concern about his son Majesty’s involvement in selling orange juice under the sun, questioning why his former partner, Michy, would engage the child in the activity when he has offices and employees. The musician said he was uncomfortable seeing Majesty exposed to the sun while selling juice, insisting that the child’s welfare should be the priority as the former couple navigate their co-parenting relationship. Speaking in an interview on Afternoon Ride with Andy Dosty on Hitz FM , Shatta Wale said he had the resources to provide opportunities for his son, including access to technology and other learning materials. “I grew up with gadgets; that’s why I am into tech, and I know how to use a computer and all those things. My kids know that, Majesty, I have bought a lot of things for him to learn,” he said. The artiste also praised Michy, describing her as a good woman whom he respected despite their separation. “Shatta Michy is a very nice woman that I met; I will always praise and give her that respect. She should have that patience that life is like that, you win some, you lose some. If we are not together, that doesn’t mean we are enemies,” he said. Shatta Wale urged his former partner to put aside their differences and focus on raising their son, stressing that whatever had happened between them was in the past. “Whatever that has happened in life has passed. What we are thinking about is the kid right now, so she should open her mind. She shouldn’t go and sit in the sun,” he stated. “Why do you want to go and stand in the sun with my son when I have offices, when I employ people?” he asked. Michy had insisted that she had never denied the musician access to Majesty and defended the child’s involvement in selling juice, describing it as his own initiative.
