items.title: One light day
items.description: ON Nov 18, 2026 (today), the National Aeronautics and Space Administration (Nasa) spacecraft, Voyager 1, the furthest travelled human-made object, launched in 1977 and since then travelling at a non-stop average speed of 61,200km per hour, will cover a distance of one light day. In Cosmos, astronomer Carl Sagan writes, “The dimensions of the cosmos are so large that using familiar units of distance, such as meters or miles, chosen for their utility on earth, would make little sense. Instead, we measure distance with the speed of light [ie the distance light travels in one year]”. Light travels at the superluminal speed of 1,079,252,848km/h, and thus is capable of orbiting the earth’s equator 7.5 times in one second. A Boeing 747, travelling at non-stop cruising speed, which is around 900km/h, would take around 3,300 years to cover a distance of one light day, and reach where Voyager 1 will be today. For the feat, you would have had to take off in a Boeing 747 in the Bronze Age, when Rameses II was ruling Egypt, and travel continuously at cruising speed to cover a distance of one light day by 2026. Your journey would have had to commence in a world before Christ, Cyrus, Caesar and Confucius. While a light day seems very far, on the cosmic scale, it is mundanely trivial. Our nearest star, Proxima Centauri, is about 4.2 light-years away. A journey Voyager 1 — according to Nasa — is expected to cover in 75,000 years, despite its hypersonic speed. Imagine what lies beyond the gaze of the naked eye. To fathom the stupefying distances, Richard Dawkins in The Magic of Reality writes, “Go out into a big field with a football and plonk it down to represent the sun [which is 1.3 million times larger than the earth in volume]. Then walk 25 metres away and drop a peppercorn to represent the Earth’s size and its distance from the sun. The moon, to the same scale, would be a pinhead, and it would be only 5 centimetres away from the peppercorn. But the nearest other star, Proxima Centauri, to the same scale, would be another (slightly smaller) football, located about six-and-a-half thousand kilometres away”. That is about the same distance from London to Chicago. We naively believe that when we gaze up into the night sky, we witness billions upon billions of stars — and perceive this as infinity. The actual number is close to 6,000, with the furthermost stars visible to the naked eye being posited no further than 15,000 light-years away. Imagine what lies beyond the gaze of the naked eye. The Milky Way galaxy, with its 100 to 400 billion stars, is estimated by Nasa to be 100,000 light-years across. Our solar system, situated about 27,000 light years from the galactic centre of the Milky Way hosting the super-giant black hole, Sagittarius A*, and orbiting it at a rate of 828,000 km/h, takes approximately 230m years to complete one galactic year. The last time our solar system was where it is now, dinosaurs had just begun to appear. In The Princeton Field Guide to Dinosaurs, Gregory S. Paul writes, “Only one galactic year ago the dinosaurs had just appeared on planet earth. When dinosaurs first appeared, our solar system was already well over 4 billion years old, and 95 per cent of the history of our planet had already passed”. Our nearest galaxy, the Andromeda galaxy with its one trillion stars, is around 2.5m light years away, what to say of the other two trillion galaxies which are spread across an observable universe with a diameter 93bn light-years across. Stephen Hawking illuminates in A Brief History of Time how Edwin Hubble’s discoveries in 1929 led to “the landmark ob­­servation that wherever you look, distant galaxies are moving rapidly away from us. In other words, the universe is expanding”. Acco­rdingly, the further galaxies are, the faster they recede, sometimes faster than the speed of light. Though nothing can travel faster than the speed of light, space can expand faster. The inference — even if we were miraculously able to travel at the speed of light, there would be parts of the universe which would be perpetually beyond our reach. We, homo sapiens, whom paleoanthropologists believe appeared 300,000 years ago, seldom view our own insignificance from this cosmic perspective. If we did, it would rob us of our prejudices, partialities and pre-conceptions. In his essay Wonder and Skepticism, Carl Sagan writes, “The truth may be puzzling. It may take some work to grapple with. It may be counterintuitive. It may contradict deeply held prejudices. It may not be consonant with what we desperately want to be true. But our preferences do not determine what’s true”. Voyager 1’s feat of travelling one light day should be a moment of pride and humility for the whole of humanity. The writer is a practising barrister. asadulmulk@legalparameter.com Published in Dawn, November 18th, 2026

items.title: £190m corruption case: IHC directs proper medical care, hygienic living conditions for Bushra Bibi as per prison rules
items.description: ISLAMABAD: The Islamabad High Court (IHC) on Wednesday directed prison authorities to ensure medical care and hygienic living conditions for Bushra Bibi as per prison rules, while adjourning the hearing of appeals filed by her and her husband, PTI founder Imran Khan, against their convictions in the £190 million case for seven days. The couple is serving prison sentences in the £190 million corruption case, also known as the Al-Qadir Trust case. On January 17, 2025, an accountability court in Islamabad sentenced Imran to 14 years in prison and Bushra to seven years in the case. Both subsequently challenged their convictions before the IHC. On Monday, Bushra had filed a fresh criminal miscellaneous application seeking the production of her complete medical record before the court and directions for her immediate transfer to a specialised hospital. A division bench comprising Chief Justice Sardar Muhammad Sarfraz Dogar and Justice Muhammad Asif granted Barrister Salman Safdar, counsel for the PTI founder, seven days to prepare arguments on the appeals. During the proceedings, the court also took up a fresh miscellaneous application filed on behalf of Bushra, raising concerns about her deteriorating eyesight, need for surgery, possible post-operative complications and the medical facilities available to her in prison. After hearing arguments from her counsel, Sardar Latif Khosa, the bench directed the prison authorities to ensure cleanliness in her cell, arrange an examination by a specialist doctor from a hospital and provide all necessary medical facilities in accordance with jail rules. The court further directed Islamabad Advocate General Naveed Hayat Malik to ensure that its order was implemented through the relevant prison authorities. Khosa informed the court that Bushra had told her legal team that she required surgery and that there were concerns about the possible deterioration of her eyesight. He stressed that Bushra’s health required immediate attention, particularly in view of the risk of infection following surgery. Reading out the contents of the miscellaneous application, Khosa also referred to incidents allegedly occurring inside the prison. He told the court that seven small snakes had reportedly been found in Bushra’s cell and killed by a prison official identified as Sibtain. The area was subsequently sealed with cement, according to the application. Khosa argued that prison conditions could expose his client to infections, making special precautions necessary, particularly if she underwent surgery. Justice Dogar said the court had taken note of the concerns and would ensure that Bushra received all facilities permissible under prison rules. He directed that the difficulties highlighted in the application should not be allowed to recur and assured Khosa that the former first lady was in safe hands. Justice Dogar also recalled that health-related matters had previously been referred to the Federal Constitutional Court (FCC), but said the present application would be dealt with in accordance with the bench’s jurisdiction. Khosa, however, maintained that the risk of infection following surgery remained a serious concern. He added that even if bail were granted, Bushra could remain in the court’s custody. When the counsel referred to the fresh application concerning Bushra’s health, Justice Dogar reminded him that he had earlier undertaken to commence arguments on the main appeals after meeting the PTI founder. Khosa confirmed that he and Barrister Safdar had met Imran in accordance with the court’s previous direction and had submitted their respective affidavits . Justice Dogar subsequently directed that arguments on the appeals commence. Khosa also informed the bench that Safdar would argue Imran’s appeal, while he would represent Bushra. Safdar requested permission to address the court and sought live broadcasting of the proceedings in the appeals, arguing that the case had attracted considerable public attention. He said that although the bench had described the matter as a routine case at the previous hearing, proceedings in the case involving former military ruler General Pervez Musharraf had been broadcast live. Referring to the live broadcasts of proceedings in various cases before the Supreme Court and high courts, Safdar urged the bench to allow the appeals to be broadcast live as well. He said he would submit a formal application in this regard. The PTI founder’s sisters, Noreen Khan and Dr Uzma, were present in the courtroom, along with PTI Chairman Barrister Gohar Ali Khan and other party leaders. National Accountability Bureau Prosecutor General Sohail Nasir, prosecutors Javed Arshad and Rafay Maqsood, and Islamabad Advocate General Naveed Hayat Malik also attended the proceedings. Tight security arrangements were in place inside and around the IHC. Barrister Safdar met Imran and Bushra at Adiala jail on Nov 2, 2026. This was his first meeting with Imran after seven months and with Bushra in 11 months, lasting 40 minutes. On Nov 11, 2026, Barrister Safdar and Khosa also met Imran and Bushra at Adiala jail for nearly three hours, following IHC orders. On Monday, both lawyers submitted affidavits to the IHC, detailing their Nov 11 meeting with the incarcerated couple at Adiala jail. The lawyers stated in their affidavits that Bushra complained of severely impaired vision in both eyes following her previous surgical procedure . She also told them that she could see only to a limited extent while wearing spectacles and was virtually unable to see without them.

items.title: EU proposes new 45bn euro Ukraine loan
items.description: The European Union on Wednesday proposed member states give Ukraine an extra 45-billion-euro ($49 billion) loan to plug Kyiv’s 2027 budget shortfalls as Russia’s war drags on. The funding would go two-thirds of the way towards filling a 70-billion-euro black hole Kyiv is facing next year — with Brussels looking to incentivise other Ukraine backers to do the rest. “Five years since the start of this war of aggression, Europe stands united. We are as committed as ever to support Ukraine in war and in peace,” European Commission chief Ursula von der Leyen said. “We think this is the best way to give Ukraine a strong hand at the negotiation table, and Ukraine only needs to repay once Russia pays for the damage it has caused in Ukraine.” EU leaders will discuss the loan at a summit in Brussels next week in the hope of reaching a deal. The EU is currently paying out a 90-billion-loan to Kyiv that it hoped would see the country through to the end of next year. But as Russia has intensified its attacks it has become clear that those funds would not be enough. The new loan would follow the same format as the current one and be borrowed against headroom in the EU’s central budget. It would also be linked to Kyiv pressing on with reforms. While the aim is to forge agreement next week, the issue of the funding has now become wrapped up with broader fraught negotiations over the EU’s next central budget. Budget brawl German Chancellor Friedrich Merz has insisted that all of the EU must settle the financing and all 27 member states must be involved before a deal can be reached on the budget. That has rankled several of the EU’s least pro-Ukraine countries who want to be left out of backing the loan, such as Bulgaria, the Czech Republic, Hungary, and Slovakia. Last time round, Budapest, Bratislava and Prague managed to get themselves exempted from having to help cover the financing. Von der Leyen insisted the aim this time remains to get all countries on board. Beyond the bloc, Brussels is pushing other allies of Ukraine – such as Britain, Canada and Japan to fill in the rest of Kyiv’s needs next year. Similar pleas have previously fallen short. In a bid to incentivise them this time, Brussels says others could provide guarantees to help bolster the loan or use the interest on frozen Russian assets in the EU to cover their own financing. The proposal for a new loan means that the EU for now won’t try to look into the thorny issue of directly tapping over 200 billion euros of frozen Russian central bank assets held in the bloc to fund Ukraine. That plan was shot down in 2025 by Belgium — where the majority of the assets are held — and the position of its government has not shifted. items.title: No one is stopping you from seeing your son; it’s a lie – Michy replies Shatta Wale
items.description: Former partner of dancehall artiste Shatta Wale, Diamond Michelle, popularly known as Shatta Michy, has accused the musician of misrepresenting their co-parenting arrangements, insisting she has never prevented him from seeing their son, Majesty. In a viral video, Michy questioned why the artiste continued to raise issues about access to their son, eight years after their relationship ended, and challenged him to put in more effort to maintain a relationship with the child. “Charles, you no tire to dey fight? You no tire to dey fight? You no tire to tell lies? It’s been eight years. What are we still fighting about there? Sweetie, what are we still fighting about?” she said. Michy maintained that her doors were always open to Shatta Wale and that she had made efforts to facilitate communication between him and Majesty, including pointing out when the musician was in their vicinity. She said she had also encouraged Majesty to communicate with his father after noticing that they had not spoken for some time. According to her, the child had complained that Shatta Wale did not answer his calls or return them, adding that she had witnessed him making several attempts to reach the musician. “I am a witness to seeing him having given you 9 or 10 missed calls,” she said, arguing that people who genuinely cared about others would return missed calls even when their phones were on do-not-disturb mode. Michy also disputed claims that she had prevented Shatta Wale from seeing Majesty despite court arrangements reportedly allowing weekend visits from Friday to Sunday. She said the musician had initially taken the child following the court order but questioned his consistency in maintaining the arrangement. “I cannot come and use a bulldozer to pull you to take care of this boy or see him on the weekends,” she said. The former partner of Shatta Wale insisted that she had not obstructed the musician’s access to their son and accused him of attempting to paint her as someone deliberately depriving him of his parental rights. READ ALSO: Shatta Wale appeals to Shatta Michy to put differences aside for son Majesty “There is not one day that you have picked up the phone to call me that I haven’t picked up. So what are you saying? Why are you always trying to paint a picture like I’m some Kakai, to wit, caricature?” she questioned. Michy also defended her son’s involvement in selling her juice, insisting that the initiative was his idea and that he was neither being forced to work nor punished. She disclosed that Majesty had created the logo for the product and said the business had generated GH¢115,000, expressing pride in his entrepreneurial initiative. “He’s a spelling bee champion. Majesty is not being forced to sell over there. I am not punishing my child,” she said. Michy described Majesty as a talented child who willingly participated in the business, explaining that he often asked permission to go out and attract customers. She said she ensured he was not exposed to excessive crowds and remained present to supervise him. According to her, the child would carry his boombox and small speaker to promote the product, attracting customers in the process. “He dey pull crowd the way you dey pull the crowd. What are you saying?” she said. Michy further questioned why Shatta Wale continued to publicly complain about being denied access to Majesty, claiming the musician had not seen the child since 2023. She said Majesty’s school was about 10 minutes away from the musician’s location and challenged him to explain what prevented him from making efforts to see the boy. “You saw this boy in 2023. You are in 2026. I want to understand. What are you complaining about? You have not made an effort,” she said. Michy accused Shatta Wale of deliberately reigniting tensions despite the circumstances surrounding their co-parenting relationship.

items.title: L’Algérie fixe la liste des réserves stratégiques d’urgence
items.description: Face à la multiplication des catastrophes naturelles dont la dernière en date a eu lieu avec les incendies dévastateurs de l’été dernier, l’Algérie se dote de réserves stratégiques. Un décret exécutif publié au dernier numéro du Journal officiel fixe la nomenclature des réserves stratégiques à constituer au niveau national, inter-wilayas et des wilayas pour une prise en charge optimale des retombées des catastrophes naturelles. La liste va des structures d’hébergement d'urgence aux fournitures scolaires, en passant par les produits alimentaires, les médicaments, les carburants… Le décret 26-353 du 8 novembre 2026 fixe la nomenclature des réserves stratégiques et les modalités de leur mise en place, de leur gestion et de leur utilisation au titre des risques de catastrophes. Algérie : comment la réserve stratégique est constituée et déployée Le texte stipule que les dépenses liées à l’acquisition, à la gestion et à l’utilisation des réserves stratégiques, ainsi qu’à la réalisation et à l’entretien des installations de leur stockage sont prises en charge par le budget de l'Etat. La réserve stratégique au niveau national est mise en place par arrêté du ministre de l’Intérieur et placée sous son autorité. Elle comprend, notamment les produits, les équipements et les fournitures entraînant des dépenses financières importantes à la charge du budget de l'Etat, précise le texte. Les réserves inter-wilayas sont désignées par arrêté du même ministre à la survenance d’une catastrophe. Elles sont constituées de l'ensemble des réserves stratégiques des wilayas pouvant apporter un soutien à la wilaya ou aux wilayas ayant un manque en réserves stratégiques. Au niveau des wilayas, la réserve stratégique est mise en place par décision du wali, et est placée sous son autorité, lit-on. La réserve stratégique peut être utilisée dans le cadre de l'aide internationale Des responsables de gestion de ces réserves sont désignés au niveau national et dans toutes les wilayas ainsi que des coordinateurs inter-wilayas. S’agissant de l’usage de la réserve stratégique au niveau national, le décret exécutif précise qu’elle est déployée par arrêté du ministre de l’Intérieur et peut être également utilisée au titre des aides humanitaires destinées à l'étranger dans le cadre de la solidarité internationale. En cas de catastrophe, le wali crée des comités chargés de recenser les sinistrés et de distribuer les produits, les équipements et les fournitures constituant les réserves stratégiques. Réserve stratégique : voici la liste des produits qui la constituent Les produits devant constituer la réserve stratégique sont détaillés dans une nomenclature jointe en annexe du décret. Il s'agit en premier lieu de l’eau (eau potable, réservoirs et réservoirs mobiles pour le stockage de l'eau et systèmes de filtration et de purification). Concernant les structures d'hébergement, il est constitué une réserve de structures temporaires d'hébergement, de lits superposés, matelas et sacs de couchage ainsi que des toilettes et douches mobiles. La liste des produits alimentaires est constituée de repas prêts à consommer, conserves, lait en poudre normal et pour nourrisson, pâtes, légumineuses, etc. Dans la même catégorie, le décret cite les équipements et matériels de cuisine, les articles et ustensiles de cuisine nécessaires, les réchauds et équipements de réfrigération. Médicaments, carburants, produits d’hygiène et fournitures scolaires… En matière de médicaments et fournitures médicales, la réserve se constitue de médicaments essentiels, dispositifs de soins spécifiques, médicaments d'urgence, médicaments pour les maladies chroniques, fournitures spécialisées pour les mesures, équipement médical, équipements et instruments pour chirurgie légère et sacs mortuaires. Des réserves de vêtements et besoins spécifiques doivent aussi être constituées. Il s'agit de vêtements nécessaires et adaptés au climat pour toutes les catégories de personnes et les différents âges. Concernant l’énergie, le décret cite les différentes sources d'énergie, les appareils de chauffage et de climatisation, les équipements de stockage de carburant et les dispositifs d'éclairage. La nomenclature contient également les fournitures d’hygiène et de nettoyage (produits d'hygiène corporelle pour toutes les catégories de personnes et les différents âges, moyens de gestion des déchets et produits de nettoyage). La dernière catégorie de produits concerne les fournitures éducatives, soit les fournitures scolaires et récréatives pour enfants. L’article L’Algérie fixe la liste des réserves stratégiques d’urgence est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: The Moderate Democrats Who Insist the Rift Is Over
items.description: After a pro-oil seminarian from Texas, a pro-gun district attorney from Mississippi, and a “pro-life with a heavy heart” megachurch pastor from Kansas picked up Senate seats for Democrats, you might have expected party centrists to do a fair bit of crowing. Yet many have instead fallen for a new kind of nonbinary politics, one that rejects the division between moderate and progressive. What was once the central fault line of party politics—epitomized by the bitter 2016 presidential primary fight between Bernie Sanders and Hillary Clinton—is now outmoded, prominent moderates are saying. “I don’t think of politics on the spectrum of left to right,” Senator Ruben Gallego, a Democrat from Arizona, told me last week at a conference in Denver. He does not care about the ideological valence of policies, he said. “We just care about the results. It’s pretty bad out there.” Instead, Gallego prefers using his own coinage to describe his politics, “big-ass-truck populism”—a program to ensure that everyone who wants a giant vehicle should be rich enough to get it. He espouses Bernie Sanders–style economic ideas (which might formerly have been called progressive), such as raising the minimum wage to $20 and increasing Social Security taxes on high-wage earners. But to actually win votes, Gallego argues, Democrats must not just redistribute; they must also avoid coastal snootiness and off-putting social-justice speak. He was an early critic of the attempted rebranding of Hispanics as “Latinx.” And the big-ass trucks he has in mind are not electric vehicles. Gallego was one of several rumored presidential candidates at a gathering this past weekend convened by Majority Democrats, a centrist group that presents itself as an alternative to the “gerontocratic establishment,” the “activist left,” and the MAGA right. Its cardinal virtues are electability and heterodoxy. Many other attendees expected to run in 2028 expressed similar irritation at the labels of “progressive” or “moderate.” Josh Shapiro, the governor of Pennsylvania, declared in his speech that, when it comes to winning over voters, “not one of them gives a damn about shallow litmus tests or where we fall on some imaginary political spectrum.” Senator Elissa Slotkin of Michigan said that “if you have elected officials who are spending all their time fighting progressive versus moderate, then they have missed the plot of the election.” The real divide, instead, would be between “team fight” and “team flight.” J. B. Pritzker, the Illinois governor, was not at the Denver conference, but he proposed a very similar typology in August : “If there’s a divide in the national Democratic Party that exists, it’s the one between team fight and team cave.” [ Read: The rise of the fusion Democrat ] Political binaries are all inexact, but survive because they are useful. Describing politicians as “right” or “left” began during the French Revolution, more than 200 years ago, when monarchists and republicans sat on opposite sides of the National Assembly. The Congressional Progressive Caucus, founded by Sanders, dates back to 1991. These ideological labels will probably not disappear in favor of sorting Democrats as either fighting or feckless. And, as the party decides where it will go in the post-Trump era, such disagreement may actually be generative. “We are about to enter the presidential primary process. And it is good for big, fractious coalitions to have debates, fights, struggles—whatever you want to call it—over our direction,” Matt Bennett of Third Way, a centrist Democratic think tank, told me on Monday. The magnanimity that Gallego, Shapiro, and others are showing might be tactical, born of the realization that progressives matter quite a lot in presidential primaries. But the reasons for the détente may also run deeper. Self-identifying as moderate in the face of such immoderate voter anger—about high prices most of all—seems incongruously timid. “I think the party not just accepts, but embraces, the premise that we are in a populist moment,” Jake Auchincloss, a Democratic representative from Massachusetts, told me. The party’s answer to economic populism, Auchincloss argued, can go one of two routes: “subsidy populism,” which involves increased government largesse and regulation, and is a recipe for inflation, or “productive populism,” which more lastingly cuts prices by eliminating bureaucracy, local land-use restrictions, and intermediaries in the health-care sector. That debate—between what I would call the “consumer socialist” wing of the party and the “abundance”-minded supply-siders—may well be the defining one of the 2028 presidential primary. [ Read: ‘Make politics boring again’ ] If moderates are inching toward progressives on economics—or at least wrapping technocratic reforms in populist packaging—the progressives have lurched toward the moderates on cultural issues, mostly by staying silent. Even if the leftmost Democrats have not entirely abandoned their beliefs, they understand that affordability politics is a better topic of discussion than abolishing prisons and capitalism and making inclusiveness involuntary through DEI policies and pronoun disclosures. “Woke 1 was crazy,” the quote popularized this year by Representative Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, is a neat encapsulation: a half-hearted mea culpa, expressing the desire to move on without too much painful reflection. Some of the worst excesses of that era—calls to defund the police and abolish immigration enforcement, attempts to rebrand mothers as “birthing people”—look unlikely to recur in the 2028 Democratic primary. Class consciousness, once the core of left-wing politics, was strangely absent from the debates over social-justice and identity politics that roiled the party for years; now it is returning to the Democratic Party. Perhaps working-class voters will, too. Only a presidential nominee can definitively settle what the post-Trump Democratic Party believes. But that will take longer than a year, and the debate will not be theoretical in the interim. “The candidates who ran for Congress and for the Senate who flipped seats did an incredible job of being very clear in some of the things they wanted to do. And now it’s going to be incumbent upon Democratic leadership to actually do those things,” Abigail Spanberger, the Democratic governor of Virginia, told me. Spanberger, who served in Congress before being elected governor in 2025, advised the new Democratic Congress to industriously pass bills reasserting control over tariffs and the Iran war and rolling back the impending changes to Medicaid that will soon remove millions from the program. Democrats who run states—herself included—must also busy themselves with their own affordability agendas on housing, health care, and energy costs, all while compensating for federal cuts to health-care and food assistance. Before the midterms, the jockeying among factions within the party led to discord over how best to challenge Republicans. Spanberger was reluctantly dragged into an effort by her party to redistrict Virginia—an effort that ultimately failed in court. With so much to do now, many in the party think the internecine squabbling should be left behind. “I think that Democrats have just won,” Spanberger said, “so we should shut the fuck up about it, and actually govern.”

items.title: Crítica de ‘GTA VI’: Bienvenidos al mayor parque de atracciones digital jamás creado
items.description: Uno solo puede escribir una crítica del GTA VI desde el pasmo . Vaya por delante que, reconociendo todos sus aciertos, a este crítico nunca le ha entusiasmado excesivamente la saga GTA —en cambio, sí siente devoción por la profundidad narrativa de Red Dead Redemption II , el wéstern crepuscular que la misma empresa, Rockstar, publicó en 2018—. Pero directamente hay que mentir para decir que uno no se siente abrumado, aplastado, por la alucinante creación digital que supone este juego y por la excepcional coherencia estética que despliega alrededor los muchos kilómetros cuadrados de su mapa. Todo parece vivo, todo está lleno de gente y actividad, todo son texturas mimadísimas, reflejos en cristales y charcos inconcebibles en cualquier otro juego, rayos de luz que hasta ahora parecían imposibles de recrear y acción e interacción en cada esquina. Lo más abrumador que el juego transmite es la sensación de que el mundo de GTA VI sigue ahí cuando dejamos de jugar, de que ese microcosmos sigue siendo coherente y autosuficiente cuando apagamos la consola. El mundo del videojuego vive un acontecimiento de época. Seguir leyendo

items.title: After 49 years in space, Voyager 1 reaches one light-day milestone
items.description: Nasa’s Voyager 1 probe, which has been travelling through space for nearly 50 years, hit a milestone distance of one light-day away from Earth on Wednesday. Already the most distant man-made object in the universe, the spacecraft is now about 26 billion kilometres (16 billion miles) away, according to the US space agency. That is the distance a particle of light can travel in 24 hours. The historic feat is “the best illustration of just how vast space is”, said Tiffany Kataria from Nasa. “So much of what we dream about is traveling to other stellar systems,” she told AFP. Participants shine lights during the “Shine Bright for Voyager’s Light-Day” celebration, marking Voyager 1 reaching one light-day from Earth, at the California Institute of Technology (Caltech) in Pasadena, California, on November 17, 2026. —AFP “And it took Voyager 1 nearly 50 years to get to just the edge of our own solar system, let alone to only a light-day.” She pointed out that many exoplanetary systems, in comparison, are at least several light-years away. Launched in 1977, Voyager 1 and its twin Voyager 2 are the only spacecraft to have reached interstellar space — the region beyond our solar system, which they continue to explore. Messages sent from Earth take about 24 hours to reach Voyager 1 and just as long for teams on the ground to receive a response. Both Voyager spacecraft carry “Golden Records” — 30-centimetre (12-inch), gold-plated copper disks intended to convey the story of our world to extraterrestrials. Some of Voyager 1’s equipment, such as cameras, has been remotely switched off to save power, but the probe continues to study invisible phenomena such as magnetic fields, Kataria said. The data it collects allows researchers like her to study “the gas, the dust and other material that exists between stars, between our Sun and other stars”. An artist’s rendering of the Voyager approaching Saturn, circa the late 1970s. —Space Fronteirs Voyagers 1 and 2 have previously explored the outer solar system, which contains the giant planets Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus and Neptune. Images of Jupiter taken by Voyager 1 first revealed the existence of rings around the gas giant and helped scientists understand the “really extreme vortices and weather that take place in the atmosphere”, Kataria said. “You could find so many things that both of these spacecraft have really enabled in our understanding”.

items.title: Blindness: Eritrea, 10 others, eliminate trachoma from Africa as Nigeria lags
items.description: By Sola Ogundipe Eritrea has become the 11th country in the World Health Organisation (WHO) African Region to eliminate trachoma as a public health problem, raising hopes of ending a neglected tropical disease (NTD) that continues to threaten the sight of millions of people across the continent. The achievement, validated by WHO, places Eritrea among 11 African countries that have successfully tackled the disease through sustained public health interventions, improved access to treatment, hygiene promotion and community mobilisation. Eritrea, Algeria, Benin, Burundi, Eritrea, The Gambia, Ghana, Malawi, Mali, Mauritania, Senegal and Togo are the African countries that have received WHO validation as the number of countries that have achieved elimination globally stands at 34. Eritrea is also the 66th country globally and the 23rd in the WHO African Region to eliminate at least one neglected tropical disease. According to WHO, Eritrea achieved the milestone, following two decades of sustained interventions targeting the disease, particularly in remote rural communities where poor access to clean water, sanitation and healthcare had fuelled its spread. Eritrea’s success followed nationwide surveys conducted between 2006 and 2020, which helped identify affected communities and guide the rollout of interventions across the country. The government subsequently implemented WHO’s recommended SAFE strategy, a combination of surgery for advanced cases, antibiotics to clear infection, facial cleanliness to limit transmission and environmental improvements, particularly better access to water and sanitation. A notable feature of the campaign was its community-led sanitation approach, which delivered significant public health gains despite limited external funding. Health workers deployed digital tools for data collection and mapping to identify affected populations, track disease patterns and direct resources to hard-to-reach communities. In a congratulatory message, WHO Director-General Dr Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus said, “I congratulate the government and people of Eritrea on this historic achievement. After two decades of determined effort, Eritrea has consigned trachoma as a public health problem to history. This is a victory for the communities most affected by this devastating disease and a powerful example of what sustained national commitment can achieve.” On his part, WHO Regional Director for Africa, Dr Mohamed Janabi, said Eritrea’s achievement demonstrated the impact of political commitment, community participation and effective partnerships in tackling neglected tropical diseases. “I congratulate Eritrea on this historic public health milestone. It shows what is possible through sustained political commitment, community leadership and strong partnerships. Eritrea’s achievement brings us closer to a world free from the suffering caused by neglected tropical diseases and sends a strong message of hope to other African countries working towards trachoma elimination,” he stated. WHO Representative to Eritrea, Dr Mary Stephen, said, “This success belongs first and foremost to the people of Eritrea. The elimination of trachoma as a public health problem is the result of strong national leadership and ownership and collaboration between communities, the Ministry of Health, the Fred Hollows Foundation, development partners and health workers across the country,” she said. While Eritrea has secured WHO validation, Nigeria is making significant progress towards eliminating trachoma, although the disease remains a public health challenge in some parts of the country. The Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare disclosed that 11 local government areas (LGAs) remained to achieve elimination status out of 134 previously identified endemic LGAs. The country has stopped mass drug administration (MDA) in 116 LGAs after they met the WHO elimination threshold, representing approximately 87 per cent progress towards eliminating the disease in affected areas. Director and Programme Manager of the National Trachoma Programme, Nicholas Olobio, said Nigeria had also performed more than 100,000 surgeries for trachomatous trichiasis, the advanced stage of the disease that can cause irreversible blindness. Nigeria’s progress has been hindered by the implementation of WHO’s SAFE strategy, supported by mass antibiotic distribution, eye surgeries, hygiene promotion and improved access to water and sanitation. Trachoma is among the 21 diseases and disease groups covered by WHO’s Neglected Tropical Diseases Roadmap 2021–2030, which seeks to accelerate prevention, control, elimination and eradication efforts, particularly among populations living in poverty and underserved communities. The disease is caused by the bacterium Chlamydia trachomatis and spreads through contact with eye and nasal discharge from infected people. Repeated infections can cause scarring of the inner eyelid, forcing the eyelashes to turn inward and scratch the eyeball. Without treatment, the condition can cause irreversible blindness. It disproportionately affects poor and underserved communities, particularly those with inadequate access to clean water, sanitation, hygiene facilities and essential healthcare. Despite significant global progress, the disease remains a public health challenge in parts of the world. Although Africa has recorded substantial progress, it remains the continent most affected by the disease. The global target for eliminating trachoma as a public health problem is part of WHO’s neglected tropical diseases roadmap for 2021 to 2030. The post Blindness: Eritrea, 10 others, eliminate trachoma from Africa as Nigeria lags appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: PM Shehbaz, PML-N supremo Nawaz discuss AJK's development, reconstruction at Muzaffarabad huddle
items.description: The PML-N’s top leadership on Wednesday discussed development and reconstruction in Azad Jammu and Kashmir (AJK) with the region’s President Muhammad Najeeb Naqi Khan and Prime Minister Syed Iftikhar Ali Gillani, the party said. The meeting, held in Muzaffarabad, was attended by Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and PML-N supremo Nawaz Sharif, who discussed public welfare, development projects and the implementation of election promises with the AJK leadership, according to a post by the party on X. Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz also attended the meeting, along with federal and provincial ministers, including Planning Minister Ahsan Iqbal and Information Minister Attaullah Tarar. The federal and Punjab governments reaffirmed their commitment to supporting AJK’s development and prosperity, the statement added. The visit comes nearly three months after the PML-N came to power in AJK in August, following phased elections in which Nawaz played an active role in the campaign. Speaking in Muzaffarabad during the election campaign in July, Nawaz had asserted that the city should be transformed into the most beautiful city of Pakistan. He said that whatever CM Maryam was doing in Lahore and other cities of Punjab should also be “copied” in Muzaffarabad and other cities of AJK. He had also promised AJK residents that every development project would be implemented and that PML-N would resolve “all the issues” if it won the elections. In his speech, he had also cautioned his party leadership in AJK that he would visit AJK every three months to see whether the party’s manifesto was being implemented. “If we win the election, I will come after every three months, and will visit each and every street with the prime minister.” After PM Gillani’s election, Nawaz handed him a comprehensive 100-day reform agenda , stressing that essential public services, including healthcare, education, sanitation and reliable roads, were basic rights of the people of AJK and should also reach remote areas rather than remain confined to major urban centres.

items.title: Beyond Fuel Prices: What investors and financiers should understand about Ghana’s downstream petroleum sector
items.description: Ghana’s downstream petroleum sector continues to attract interest from operators, banks, investors, asset managers and entrepreneurs, but investment decisions in the sector require a much broader assessment than fuel prices and headline profitability. A downstream petroleum business may report strong revenues and margins, yet still carry material risks relating to licensing, product losses, working capital, environmental liabilities, HSSE, governance, credit exposure and the reliability of operational and financial data. These risks can directly affect cash flow, debt-servicing capacity, enterprise value and ultimately the sustainability of an investment. For financial institutions and investors, this means that analysing a downstream petroleum company should go beyond reviewing its financial statements. Lenders need to understand what could interrupt the borrower’s ability to generate cash, while investors need to assess whether reported earnings are sustainable and what additional liabilities or capital requirements may emerge after an investment is made. Similarly, existing industry operators need strong controls around inventory, pricing, credit, logistics, regulatory reporting and governance to protect profitability and preserve their licence to operate. Against this background, O.C Brent International Ltd is organising an Executive Industry Briefing on Investing in Ghana’s Downstream Oil and Gas Sector, bringing together downstream operators, bankers, financiers, investors, asset managers and prospective market entrants. The session will examine how regulatory, operational, financial and governance risks interact and how these factors should influence lending, investment and management decisions. The briefing is also intended to provide participants with a practical perspective on what financiers and investors should look for before committing capital to a downstream petroleum business. The Executive Industry Briefing is scheduled for 8 December, from 8:30 a.m. to 2:00 p.m. Participation is free but strictly by invitation. Interested institutions and individuals may contact O.C Brent International Ltd on 024 968 6802 or 024 457 3604 and complete registration at ocbrent.com. The session will provide an opportunity for industry participants and providers of capital to engage on the risks, controls and investment considerations that increasingly shape value in Ghana’s downstream petroleum sector.

items.title: Burkina Faso : Le ministère en charge des Ressources animales s’assure du bon déroulement de la formation de 1 000 bassecouriers et gestionnaires de fermes à l’ENAFA
items.description: Une mission du ministère de l’Agriculture, de l’Eau et des Ressources animales et halieutiques s’est rendue, le 16 novembre 2026, à l’École nationale de formation agricole (ENAFA). Conduite par le directeur général des services vétérinaires, le capitaine vétérinaire Aboubacar Nacro, elle est venue s’assurer du bon déroulement de la formation de 1 000 bassecouriers et gestionnaires de fermes, entamée le 25 octobre dernier. ​À cette occasion, les membres de la mission ont partagé la routine matinale des apprenants, entre course sportive, exercices d’étirement et montée des couleurs nationales. Une immersion qui leur a permis de toucher du doigt les conditions de séjour et de formation des bénéficiaires. ​Au nom du ministre d’État, le capitaine vétérinaire Aboubacar Nacro a souligné que cette initiative vise à pallier le manque de personnel qualifié dans les fermes avicoles, dont plusieurs sont à l’arrêt faute de compétences suffisantes en gestion et en suivi. Il a invité les apprenants à faire preuve d’assiduité afin de contribuer au renforcement de la production avicole nationale. ​Les participants ont, pour leur part, exprimé leur satisfaction quant à la qualité des enseignements reçus. Prenant la parole, Imelda Joellie Ouédraogo a indiqué que cette formation va contribuer à améliorer leur production. « Nous avons appris les mesures de biosécurité, les normes concernant la gestion des poulaillers et à gérer correctement l’aliment pour pouvoir rentabiliser la production qui sera effectuée », a-t-elle expliqué. ​Se réjouissant de l’intérêt manifesté par les bénéficiaires, le directeur général des productions animales, Émilien Bakoné, les a exhortés à mettre en pratique les compétences acquises dès leur retour dans leurs localités respectives. ​« Nous sommes là pour les encourager pour qu’à la fin de cette formation, ils puissent disposer de toutes les connaissances nécessaires pour permettre donc d’accroître la production avicole » , a-t-il ajouté. ​Toutefois, les participants ont lancé un appel à l’endroit des autorités pour un accompagnement à l’issue de la formation, pour promouvoir leurs activités avicoles à l’issue de cette formation. Faso7 L’article Burkina Faso : Le ministère en charge des Ressources animales s'assure du bon déroulement de la formation de 1 000 bassecouriers et gestionnaires de fermes à l'ENAFA est apparu en premier sur Faso7 .

items.title: Aide sociale directe : 1.460 ménages bénéficient déjà de la prime destinée à encourager l’emploi déclaré
items.description: L’Agence nationale du soutien social (ANSS) a annoncé le versement des premières tranches de la prime exceptionnelle destinée aux ménages bénéficiaires de l’Aide sociale directe (ASD) qui s’engagent dans une activité professionnelle déclarée. À fin octobre 2026, 1.460 demandes avaient été acceptées sur plus de 1.970 enregistrées, soit un taux d’acceptation de 74 %. Les premières tranches de la prime exceptionnelle destinée à encourager l’insertion professionnelle dans le secteur formel ont été versées aux ménages bénéficiaires de l’Aide sociale directe dont le chef de ménage ou l’un des conjoints a commencé une activité déclarée auprès de la Caisse nationale de sécurité sociale (CNSS), a précisé l'Agence. Depuis l’entrée en vigueur de ce dispositif, instauré par la loi n° 041.26 modifiant et complétant la loi n° 58.23 relative au régime de l’ASD, plus de 1.970 demandes ont été déposées. Parmi elles, 1.460 ont reçu un avis favorable, correspondant à un taux d’acceptation de 74 %. La moitié des ménages bénéficiaires de cette prime résident en milieu rural. La mesure vise à encourager les bénéficiaires de l’aide sociale à accéder à un emploi déclaré, sans craindre de perdre immédiatement leur soutien financier en intégrant le marché du travail formel. Une prime versée pendant douze mois Le montant de cette prime exceptionnelle est équivalent à celui de l’aide dont bénéficie le ménage dans le cadre du régime de l’ASD. Elle est accordée pendant douze mois, de manière continue ou discontinue, à compter de la date d’immatriculation du chef de ménage ou de l’un des conjoints au régime de sécurité sociale. La demande doit être déposée par le chef de ménage sur le portail électronique dédié www.asd.ma . L’ANSS invite ainsi les bénéficiaires qui souhaitent accéder à un emploi déclaré à effectuer les démarches nécessaires pour vérifier leur éligibilité et solliciter cette prime. Le dispositif repose sur deux mécanismes introduits par la loi n° 041.26. Le premier prévoit le versement de cette prime exceptionnelle pendant la période d’intégration professionnelle. Le second permet au ménage de retrouver immédiatement le bénéfice de l’Aide sociale directe en cas de perte de l’emploi déclaré du chef de ménage ou de l’un des conjoints, sans devoir attendre le délai de douze mois normalement prévu par la loi n° 58.23. Éviter que l’accès à l’emploi entraîne une perte immédiate de l’aide Ces deux mesures répondent à une difficulté relevée depuis le lancement du programme d’Aide sociale directe : certains ménages hésitaient à intégrer le marché du travail formel par crainte de perdre leur éligibilité à l’aide dès leur déclaration auprès de la CNSS. Une étude de terrain menée par l’ANSS auprès des bénéficiaires apporte un éclairage sur leurs attentes. Selon ses résultats, 60 % des personnes interrogées se disent disposées à renoncer à l’aide en contrepartie d’un emploi stable. Par ailleurs, 40 % souhaitent bénéficier d’un accompagnement vers l’insertion professionnelle ou la création d’une activité génératrice de revenus. L’Agence a également procédé à une segmentation statistique des bénéficiaires afin d’identifier les catégories présentant un potentiel d’insertion socio-économique. Trois groupes ont ainsi été distingués : les « Foyers émergents », qui regroupent 1.209.436 ménages, les « Foyers en mue », qui en comptent 986.265, ainsi que les « Solitaires sans relais », représentant 156.936 personnes. Ces catégories représentent plus de 60 % de l’ensemble des ménages bénéficiaires de l’Aide sociale directe et concentrent 84 % des bénéficiaires de la prime exceptionnelle à fin octobre 2026. Pour l’ANSS, cette prime doit constituer un filet de sécurité financière temporaire pendant la période d’accès à l’emploi formel. Elle vise à éviter une rupture brutale des revenus et à préserver la continuité de la protection sociale des ménages concernés, afin de soutenir leur autonomie économique et sociale. L’Agence rappelle enfin que les bénéficiaires de l’ASD peuvent vérifier leur éligibilité à cette prime à travers ses canaux de communication officiels. The post Aide sociale directe : 1.460 ménages bénéficient déjà de la prime destinée à encourager l’emploi déclaré appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Figure de l’excellence universitaire : Vitagro rend hommage au Pr Aminata Sall Diallo
items.description: Faire de la formation un véritable levier de transformation du secteur agricole. C’est l’ambition de Novagri à travers Vitagro, son centre d’excellence et de formation implanté à Keur Pathé, dans la commune de Mboro. Axée sur la recherche, l’innovation, l’agro-industrie et le développement durable, cette infrastructure entend contribuer à la souveraineté alimentaire et à la modernisation de l’agriculture sénégalaise. L’originalité du centre repose sur une approche pédagogique alliant enseignements théoriques et apprentissage pratique, afin de préparer les apprenants aux réalités des métiers agricoles. Ses activités s’articulent autour de quatre filières principales : le lait, l’aviculture, la pisciculture et l’agriculture. Le dispositif comprend également la valorisation des espèces végétales rares ou menacées. Le lancement officiel des activités a été présidé, le lundi 16 novembre 2026, à Dakar, par le ministre de l’Agriculture, le Dr Cheikh Oumar Ba. Saluant la pertinence de cette initiative, il a exprimé la volonté de l’État d’accompagner un projet en phase avec les ambitions nationales en matière de souveraineté alimentaire. A lire aussi : Popularité et compétence (Par Aly DIOUF) La cérémonie a également été marquée par un hommage au Pr Aminata Sall Diallo, agrégée de physiologie, dont le nom a été attribué à la première promotion. Figure reconnue du monde universitaire, elle s’est illustrée par son engagement dans la transmission du savoir et la formation de générations d’universitaires, dont plusieurs sont devenus recteurs. Intitulée « Du savoir à l’impact : former pour transformer l’agriculture et la société », sa leçon inaugurale a mis en lumière le rôle stratégique de l’agriculture moderne dans les politiques de formation. Elle a notamment rappelé la nécessité de renforcer les enseignements professionnalisants pour mieux répondre aux besoins du secteur et accompagner les ambitions de développement du pays. Aly DIOUF

items.title: Deux mois de mobilisations : la colère gronde chez les CRS épuisés
items.description: Apres deux mois de mobilisations sociales intenses, les Compagnies republicaines de securite (CRS) montrent des signes de rupture. Le 17 novembre, a l'occasion d'une nouvelle journee d'action dans la fonction publique, des centaines d'agents, pres d'un millier selon les syndicats, ont fait valoir leur droit a consulter un medecin. Dans une profession privee du droit de greve, le recours massif s'apparente a une de grogne inedite depuis plusieurs annees tandis que le mouvement social, et donc la mobilisation securitaire, se poursuit en France . Un signal d'alarme dans les unites de premiere ligne Les chiffres communiques par les organisations professionnelles sont eloquents. Une trentaine de compagnies sur les 63 que compte le pays auraient ete touchees. La CRS 8, unite specialisee dans les interventions rapides, a vu la totalite de ses effectifs se declarer en consultation, rendant son deploiement impossible. a Marseille, aucune unite n'etait disponible ; dans le Var, 64 agents sur 73 de la compagnie 59 manquaient a l'appel ; a Bordeaux, deux compagnies sur trois etaient immobilisees. Sur X, Linda Kebbab, secretaire nationale d'Un1te, a resume la situation : « Des centaines de policiers CRS epuises n'ont pu prendre leur service ce matin et sont contraints de consulter leur medecin. [...] Au ministere, ils n'ont pas vu arriver ce mouvement majeur d'epuisement et de colere de ceux que nous representons alors que nous les prevenons depuis des mois. » Des centaines de policiers CRS épuisés n’ont pu prendre leur service ce matin et sont contraints de consulter leur médecin. Les personnels non-actifs c’est à dire administratifs, techniques, et spécialisés sont en grève grâce à l’appel de FO et UN1TÉ. Au ministère, ils n’ont pas vu arriver ce mouvement majeur d’épuisement et de colère de ceux que nous représentons alors que nous les prévenons depuis des mois. Visiblement nos hauts responsables sont aussi visionnaires et aptes à analyser, qu’ils l’ont été pour prévenir les violences du 17 octobre. — Linda Kebbab (@LindaKebbab) November 17, 2026 Les raisons avancees sont multiples. Les agents evoquent des journees de 13 a 15 heures, parfois sur 17 jours consecutifs, des week-ends passes loin de chez eux et une violence accrue lors des heurts. Plus de 1 000 policiers et gendarmes ont ete blesses depuis le debut de la contestation tandis que les forces de police ont ete mises en cause pas des journalistes pour des faits de violences . Sur les ondes de Sud Radio le 18 novembre, Olivier Cappe, secretaire national d'Un1te CRS, a parle d'un « point de rupture » et « La resilience a ses limites. La corde a craque, on avait prevenu. Il y a un manque de consideration inacceptable ». 👮"Des collègues ont lâché..." Fatigue, violences, les CRS tirent la sonnette d'alarme ! 🗣️Olivier Cappe (@UN1TECRS) : "La résilience a ses limites. La corde a craqué, on avait prévenu. Il y a un manque de considération inacceptable" #GrandMatin 📻https://t.co/LIMgdJS9Le https://t.co/U4lAnI0pkJ — Sud Radio (@SudRadio) November 18, 2026 La colere s'est cristallisee apres une rencontre, le 13 novembre, avec Laurent Nuñez. Les syndicats reclamaient une hausse immediate de l'indemnite de sujetion speciale de police (ISSP), passee de 28,5 % a 35 % du traitement. Le ministere n'a propose qu'une revalorisation progressive : 1 point en 2027, puis 2 points en 2028 et 2029. Le syndicat Alliance Police nationale a deja annonce une « journee noire » le 26 novembre avec un appel a manifestation nationale.

items.title: Loi sur la profession d’avocat : les barreaux ne désarment pas
items.description: L’Association des barreaux du Maroc campe sur son refus du texte régissant la profession d’avocat et annonce une série d’actions. Colloque international à Rabat, procès simulé de la loi, rassemblements devant les cours d’appel et arrêt de travail figurent au programme. L’Association des barreaux du Maroc n’entend pas céder. Dans un communiqué, elle réaffirme son opposition à la loi n° 66.23 relative à la profession d’avocat et précise qu’elle ne renoncera à aucune de ses revendications professionnelles. Elle ne se résigne pas non plus aux dispositions qui cristallisent le différend. Elle promet de se battre par toutes les voies possibles jusqu’à ce que le texte soit amendé. Le communiqué formule un réquisitoire sévère contre le texte. Selon l’Association, il porte atteinte aux droits acquis des avocats et foule aux pieds les principes universels de la profession. Il fragilise également son indépendance, son immunité et sa capacité à se gérer elle-même. Les barreaux reprochent aussi au texte d'affaiblier la place de l’avocat dans l’architecture judiciaire. Face à l’accusation et au juge, la défense constitue un contrepoids indispensable, soulignent-ils, et cet équilibre est l’un des fondements d’un État démocratique respectueux des droits humains. L’Association va plus loin sur le plan juridique. Elle affirme que la loi renferme des dispositions inapplicables, contradictoires entre elles et contraires à la Constitution. Elle juge qu’une intervention urgente s’impose pour les corriger, d’autant que leur entrée en vigueur plongerait la profession dans une crise institutionnelle sans précédent. Les avocats annoncent par ailleurs qu’ils poursuivront leur travail de plaidoyer auprès des composantes de la majorité comme de l’opposition. Ils les exhortent à prendre leurs responsabilités historiques et à rectifier le tir, en s’appuyant sur l’objectivité, le respect de la Constitution et des principes universels de la profession. Ils invoquent aussi l’intérêt du citoyen, qui a besoin d’une défense forte, libre et indépendante. Une telle défense garantirait l’équilibre au sein de la justice et servirait au mieux l’intérêt supérieur de la nation, dans le respect de la loi et des droits, ainsi que dans la consolidation de la démocratie de l’État. Le plaidoyer s’accompagne d’un calendrier de mobilisation. L’Association organisera le 11 décembre prochain, à Rabat, un colloque international consacré à cette loi, au cours duquel un procès simulé du texte sera mis en scène. Elle appelle en outre tous les barreaux à marquer la Journée nationale de l’avocat, qui tombe le dimanche 29 novembre, par des rassemblements locaux devant les cours d’appel. Le lendemain, 30 novembre, les avocats cesseront le travail pendant une heure, et des actions de protestation seront organisées. L’Association précise enfin que son président a remis au ministre de la Justice, lors d’une récente rencontre, un mémorandum détaillé. Ce document recense les modifications à apporter au texte. Elles concernent d’abord l’immunité, l’indépendance, les missions des institutions professionnelles et leurs rapports avec le ministère public. Elles portent aussi sur l’autogestion de la profession. items.title: Classement FIFA : le Maroc intègre le Top5 mondial
items.description: Les Lions de l'Atlas continuent d'écrire les plus belles pages de leur histoire. Grâce à leurs récentes performances lors de la trêve internationale de novembre, l'équipe nationale du Maroc s'est hissée pour la première fois à une impressionnante 5e place au classement mondial de la FIFA, avec un total de 1 805,34 points. Cette ascension a été rendue possible par les solides résultats de la sélection nationale, conjugués aux récents faux pas de concurrents directs tels que le Brésil et le Portugal. En intégrant le très fermé Top 5 mondial, le Maroc confirme non seulement sa suprématie sur le continent africain et dans le monde arabe, mais égale aussi le record historique pour une nation africaine dans ce classement (détenu jusqu'ici par le Nigeria depuis avril 1994). Une dynamique exceptionnelle qui confirme le statut des Lions de l'Atlas parmi les plus grandes puissances du football mondial. Le Top 5 mondial reste composé de grandes nations du football. L'Espagne conserve la première place avec 2 004,48 points, devant l'Argentine, deuxième, et la France, troisième. L'Angleterre occupe le quatrième rang après sa victoire 3-2 face à l'Espagne. Le Maroc s'installe ainsi juste derrière ce quatuor européen et sud-américain, mais devant le Portugal, le Brésil et la Belgique. items.title: Nigerian Artist Wins Global Super Group ‘Art of the Game’ Competition, Securing £10,000 Donation for Lagos Charity
items.description: Super Group, the parent company of leading sportsbook brand Betway, has announced Nigerian artist Omomurewa Alade as the winner of its global Art of the Game competition. In recognition of her creative achievement, Alade received a £10,000 cash prize, while an additional £10,000 was donated to her chosen charity, the Feed the Widows Project in Lagos. Launched by Super Group earlier this year, Art of the Game invited artists from around the world to create a custom basketball design inspired by their culture, identity and personal creative vision. The competition was designed to celebrate the connection between sport, art and community, while creating a lasting impact beyond the competition itself. Alade’s winning design stood out among entries submitted from across the globe, impressing judges with its creativity, originality and representation of cultural identity. As part of her prize, Alade received £10,000, while a further £10,000 donation was awarded to Feed the Widows Project, a Lagos-based organisation dedicated to supporting widows and vulnerable members of the community. The donation forms part of Super Group Cares, the company’s global social impact programme focused on empowering communities and creating meaningful opportunities around the world. Kirsty Ross, Chief Operating Officer at Super Group, commented: “Art of the Game was created to celebrate the powerful connection between sport, creativity and community. Omomurewa Alade’s design captured that spirit brilliantly, and we’re delighted that her success will also make a meaningful difference through Feed the Widows Project. Through Super Group Cares, we remain committed to supporting initiatives that create lasting impact in the communities where we operate.” Representatives from Feed the Widows Project welcomed the donation, highlighting the positive impact it will have on the organisation’s ongoing programmes and outreach efforts. Since launching earlier this year, Art of the Game has showcased the creativity and diversity of artists from around the world, demonstrating how sport can inspire artistic expression while helping to deliver meaningful community impact. The competition culminates with Alade being recognised as the inaugural Art of the Game winner, with her success serving as a reminder that creativity has the power not only to connect people across cultures and continents, but also to create positive change where it is needed most. – ENDS – About Super Group Super Group (SGHC) Limited is a holding company for a leading global online sports betting brand (Betway) and multi-brand gaming businesses (Spin). The group is licensed in multiple jurisdictions, with leading positions in key markets throughout Europe, North America and Africa. The group’s sports betting and online gaming offerings are underpinned by its scale and leading technology, enabling agile operation and execution in a diverse range of markets. Its proprietary marketing and data analytics engine empowers it to responsibly provide a unique and personalized customer experience. Super Group was placed at number 5 in the latest EGR Power 50 rankings. For more information, visit www.supergroup.com . items.title: Iran, allies hit Gulf countries after US attack on island
items.description: Gulf nations scrambled to intercept incoming fire on Wednesday, after Iran and its allies lashed out following a US strike on a strategic island, in attacks that threatened to derail efforts to end the war. Kuwait activated its air defences to counter drone strikes – the first since early September – and Bahrain said it fended off an Iranian attack, after the United States struck Iran’s Qeshm Island in the flashpoint Strait of Hormuz. Explosions were heard in Saudi Arabia, the world’s biggest crude oil exporter, which said it intercepted a cruise missile fired by the Iran-backed Houthis, who have been seizing fresh territory in neighbouring Yemen. Bahrain has now suffered four Iranian attacks in six days, ending a weeks-long respite in the war that started with US-Israeli strikes on the Islamic republic on February 28. Iran responded by striking America’s wealthy Gulf allies, which host US military bases, and blockading Hormuz, which before the war carried a quarter of global oil flows. The Iranian army said “combat and kamikaze drones” targeted US air defence systems and launch platforms at Kuwait’s Ali Al-Salem air base on Wednesday. A day earlier, American fighter jets hit a missile launch site on Qeshm Island with “precision munitions”, a US military official said, describing it as a riposte to Iranian aggression. ‘Dangerous escalation’ Iran’s army chief Amir Hatami warned of a “more devastating” reaction to America and its allies. “Should the enemy make a mistake and repeat actions that have previously led them to despair, our response — directed at both the enemy and their backers — will undoubtedly be even more devastating and will know no geographical boundaries,” Hatami said, according to Iran’s Fars news agency. Mediator Qatar, which held talks with Iranian officials on Tuesday, called the latest attacks a “dangerous escalation” and warned they undercut efforts to find a peaceful solution. “The continuation of these attacks represents a dangerous escalation that could complicate efforts to contain tensions and undermine political and diplomatic efforts aimed at ensuring the security and stability of the region,” a foreign ministry statement said. Kuwaiti residents described feelings of foreboding as attacks returned to the tiny, oil-rich country, which was hit hard by Iranian strikes earlier in the war. “The explosions seemed to be coming from far away, but hearing them again after a period of calm was both surprising and worrying,” said Egyptian resident Hani Mohammed, 40. “People had started to readjust to a normal life. The sounds of planes and explosions no longer set the pace of daily life as before. But what happened has revived feelings of anxiety.” Windows rattled Meanwhile, one seafarer was missing after a ship belonging to ADNOC, the United Arab Emirates’ oil giant, was struck late on Tuesday in Hormuz, the company said. Ships transiting Hormuz have come under nearly daily fire from Iran, which insists they use routes it has authorised. The US has responded by imposing a blockade on Iranian ports, and its navy escorts tankers through the narrow passage. Saudi Arabia has endured weeks of attacks by the Houthis, who have completed their control of Yemen’s Red Sea coast and advanced close to the government’s interim capital, Aden. A four-year truce in Yemen’s bloody civil war, where a Saudi-led coalition has fought for the government since 2015, dissolved in July. On Wednesday, an “extremely loud” explosion was heard in the north of the Saudi capital Riyadh, a resident told AFP. Another said windows rattled throughout their house, while doors flew open and lights flickered. Earlier, Saudi coalition spokesman Turki al-Malki posted on X that “a cruise missile, launched by the terrorist Houthi militia toward the Riyadh area, has been intercepted and destroyed”. At the cheque presentation ceremony, Promasidor Ghana’s Chief Executive Officer (CEO), Samir Sadaoui, said the initiative reflects Promasidor’s belief that corporate success should come with meaningful contributions to society, especially in areas that directly affect people’s lives and well-being. Screenshot “Our latest intervention builds on our longstanding partnership with Cardio, where we donated a total of GH¢825,600 between 2023 and 2024, supporting 15 financially disadvantaged patients to access critical cardiac surgeries,” he added. “At Promasidor Ghana, we believe that business success must go hand in hand with social responsibility. This contribution is also our way of expressing gratitude to the good people of Ghana for their continued trust and loyalty, which have helped make our brands household names across the country.” The Director of the NCTC, Dr Kow Entsua-Mensah, commended Promasidor Ghana for its sustained support. “When our patients get diagnosed, but there is no money to fund the surgery, it becomes very difficult for both the doctor and the family. He revealed that all 15 patients previously supported through the partnership have undergone successful surgeries and have returned to normal health, with occasional clinic visits to monitor their recovery. He said this outcome shows the tangible impact of the collaboration and underscores the importance of sustained private-sector support for specialised healthcare.

items.title: Assemblée nationale : examen du projet de budget 2027
items.description: Les députés sont convoqués en séance plénière ce mercredi 18 novembre 2026 à 10 H 00. L’ordre du jour porte sur l’examen du projet de budget 2027. Selon un communiqué de l’Assemblée nationale, les points suivants seront abordés. Il s’agit notamment des considérations générales ; de l’examen des recettes ; du plafond des autorisations des dépenses du budget général et des autorisations des opérations d’emprunt, à savoir la dette publique. Il convient de noter que, concernant le projet de loi de finances initiale (LFI) 2027, aucun budget des différents ministères n’a été voté en commission par les députés de Pastef qui composent la majorité de l’hémicycle. A lire aussi : LFR 2026 : les députés rejettent les deux amendements présentés par le gouvernement ainsi que le projet de loi Ainsi, après le rejet de la loi de finances rectificative 2026 et ces rejets en commission, on peut s’attendre à ce que l’Assemblée nationale n’adopte pas la LFI 2027. Il urge de relever que face à cette situation, l’État dispose d’autres mécanismes pour contourner le vote de l’Assemblée nationale. En fait, l'article 86, alinéa 6 de la Constitution du Sénégal permet au Premier ministre d'engager la responsabilité du gouvernement devant l'Assemblée nationale sur l'adoption d'un texte de loi, rendant le texte adopté sauf vote d'une motion de censure dans les 24 heures. Le chef de l’État a également la possibilité de dissoudre l'Assemblée nationale dès le 2 décembre prochain et de convoquer de nouvelles élections législatives dans les prochains mois. Mariama DIEME

items.title: Benue North East: Court declares Suswam as APC valid senatorial candidate
items.description: The Federal High Court in Abuja on Wednesday declared former Governor of Benue, Gabriel Suswam, as the valid candidate of the All Progressives Congress (APC) for the 2027 Benue North East senatorial election. Justice Inyang Ekwo, in a judgment, agreed with the argument of the ex-governor that he was unlawfully substituted by the party, having won the majority of the valid votes cast. Justice Ekwo held that the substitution was not in synch with the provisions of the Electoral Act and the 1999 Constitution (as amended), including the APC’s Constitution. The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that Suswam had, in the suit marked FHC/ABJ/CS/1470/2026, prayed the court to recognise him as the validly elected candidate of the APC for the senatorial district. The former governor joined the APC, incumbent Sen. Emmanuel Udenbe and INEC as defendants in the suit. At the last proceedings, counsel to INEC, Anthony Malik, SAN, told the court that documents relating to the conduct of the primary indicated that Suswam won the exercise. Malik urged the court to determine the dispute in accordance with the result of the primary election, maintaining that the electoral body had placed before the court its report on the exercise, as well as the result. He consequently asked the court to uphold the outcome showing Suswam as the winner of the primary. Suswam’s counsel, Jibrin Okutepa, SAN, also urged the court to grant the reliefs sought by his client. Okutepa asked the court to reject the preliminary objections raised against the suit by the APC and Udenbe, arguing that the objections lacked merit. However, counsel to the APC, A. G. Yirvoms, asked the court to uphold the party’s preliminary objection and dismiss Suswam’s case. Suswam is challenging the decision of the APC to hand its Benue North East senatorial ticket to Udenbe despite his claim that he won the party’s primary election. (NAN) The post Benue North East: Court declares Suswam as APC valid senatorial candidate appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Humans Have Crossed a New Threshold in Space
items.description: For 4.5 billion years, Earth’s relationship with the cosmos involved only stuff falling onto our planet from space. Back when Earth was just a small pile of rocks, it grew thanks to torrents of additional rocks raining down upon it. Later, the water of our oceans was likely delivered by comets and asteroids, which also dispensed starter packs of organic molecules that may have been essential to getting life going. And then, just recently, Earth reversed the flow. About 70 years ago, humans packed small boxes of electronics—the first satellites—into rockets and blasted them into orbit. Now we’ve stuffed Earth’s orbit to the gills and visited every planet in the solar system with our robot emissaries. We’ve even sent out probes that will one day travel beyond the sun’s reach. This morning, around a quarter past 5, one of those probes crossed a milestone at that frontier, passing one light-day of distance from its home world. Voyager 1 had already traveled farther from Earth than had any other human artifact. But its light-day journey is a reminder that living beings on this planet are capable of not only escaping its boundaries but also reaching back out to the universe that made life here possible. Voyager 1 took nearly 50 years to cover that distance, which is about 16 billion miles. NASA launched the craft and its twin, Voyager 2, in 1977 to complete a “Grand Tour” of the outer solar system, which was at that point largely unexplored. The images the Voyager probes sent back of Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, and Neptune were groundbreaking. But getting the Voyagers out that far meant that they could never come back and would instead embark on an endless journey into interstellar space. In case anyone ever came across the lonely crafts, each one carried the “Golden Record,” a metal LP inscribed with sounds from Earth, including greetings in 55 languages and Chuck Berry’s “Johnny B. Goode.” Outside the solar system, where the Voyager probes are headed, astronomers measure distance in terms of how far light—the fastest thing in the universe—travels in a given interval. The distance to other stars, for example, is measured in light-years, each of which is almost 6 trillion miles. The mind withers before such numbers; a light-year represents more than 200 million flights around the Earth. Here, however, is the real kicker: One light-year doesn’t get you to even our next-door neighbor, cosmically speaking. The closest star, Alpha Centauri, is about four-and-a-half light-years away. Most other suns in the vast city of stars we call the Milky Way are hundreds, thousands, or even hundreds of thousands of light-years from our own. Scientists and science writers sometimes say that Voyager 1 (which travels slightly ahead of Voyager 2) is the first space probe to leave the solar system, but by the strictest measure, one light-day is still well within the boundaries of Earth’s home. Back in 2012, Voyager 1 crossed the heliopause, the boundary between the so-called solar wind of particles streaming off the sun’s surface and the interstellar gas atoms the solar system is flying through. It’s an important boundary, but not really the end of the solar system. That honor rests with the Oort cloud, a shell of frozen comet hearts that defines the true outer wards of the sun’s gravitational empire. Depending on how you measure it, the Oort cloud begins at about 20 light-days from Earth and extends to almost 600 light-days at its outer reaches. In this context, Voyager 1 has barely made it to the front door of our cosmic house. But focusing on distance alone obscures the real significance of Voyager 1’s journey. Consider that, ever since the very first organism appeared some 3.5 billion to 4 billion years ago, every cell on Earth has come from another cell before it. Life on our planet forms an unbroken lineage, one cell passing its vitality and know-how on to the next. We humans like to congratulate ourselves on how smart we are. We’ve probed the atom, discovered the blueprint for life, built machines that can escape not only Earth’s gravitational tyranny but, eventually, the sun’s too. But we owe it all to the many nameless microscopic blobs, crawling sea things, and giant, furry whatevers that came before us, each of which owed its own existence to ancient space debris. That means that every threshold Voyager 1 crosses is not just a human achievement but also the multibillion-year project of the entire living planet. Reversing the downward flow of accretion onto Earth and offering in return a small outward push toward the stars can be seen as Earth’s biosphere calling out to the universe. If life is common out there among the oceans of starlight, then perhaps many of its instantiations have had their own version of this Voyager 1 milestone, sending symbols of their own hope and gratitude a light-day away. In that case, Voyager 1’s light-day journey could serve as a signal that Earth is ready to join the universe’s other communities of sentience and wisdom. In the span of less than a century, humans have initiated what will hopefully be a long era of expansion outward. As a species and as representatives of Earth’s collective life, we have been driven to search for sentience beyond our home planet and to spread it beyond our own borders. It is, perhaps, the greatest thanks Earth can offer to the universe that has spent so many billions of years nurturing it. * Illustration sources: Corbis / Getty ; Heritage Space / Heritage Images / Getty ; Oxford Science Archive / Print Collector / Getty ; Smith Collection / Gado / Getty.

items.title: La humanidad cruza una nueva frontera: la ‘Voyager 1’ ya está a un día luz de la Tierra
