items.title: Nvidia says no return for ousted CEO, reports revenue boom
items.description: US chip giant Nvidia on Tuesday ruled out any comeback for ousted CEO Jensen Huang, who was forced out in a spy scandal, and reported that it had doubled revenue in the third quarter to more than $115 billion, beating expectations. Huang sought to be reinstated despite resigning last week over an affair with an alleged Chinese spy, but his successor — interim CEO Colette Kress — said that it was now “business as usual” at the company as it charts a way ahead without him. Harvey Jones, the chair of the company’s board, said in an earnings call that “the Nvidia board unanimously accepted his resignation and does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO.” Investors scoured the upbeat results for evidence that the artificial intelligence boom can withstand the Nvidia crisis, which highlighted a loophole allegedly exploited by Chinese companies. “Our momentum is real. Nvidia is an exceptional technology leader, powered by the relentless innovation of our people,” Kress said in her first remarks since being appointed by the board last week. She forecast stronger revenue growth of 75 percent in next fiscal year, up from 70 percent. Huang’s bid on Tuesday to get his job back was the latest twist for the company at the center of an AI boom that has propelled markets to record highs and boosted global economic growth. The recent upheaval has battered shares of Nvidia — which has lost $700 billion in market value since the scandal broke — and Huang is to be questioned by US lawmakers on December 1 over national security concerns. A charismatic promoter of AI, his fall triggered immediate calls from Elon Musk and others for his return, and even President Donald Trump said he “would not mind” seeing Huang back at Nvidia, downplaying the espionage allegations. – Battle over AI chips – “Since my departure, I’ve seen an outpouring of calls from Nvidia’s employees, investors, business partners, and customers for me to return as CEO,” Huang said, hours before the earnings release. “If the Board of Directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America, I would be honored to answer these calls and return as CEO.” As the spy scandal deepened, Washington on Monday announced new restrictions on AI chip exports, drawing condemnation from Beijing. The new US export curbs and the wider Nvidia scandal risk casting a shadow over talks between Trump and Chinese leader Xi Jinping at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit, which starts this week in the Chinese city of Shenzhen. Under Washington’s new rules, data centers anywhere in the world will need a US license to provide large volumes of computing power from advanced chips to companies headquartered in China, Macau or other countries under US arms embargoes. The rules also require licenses to ship advanced chips to Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia and Brazil — countries the US Commerce Department says present a “higher-than-normal risk of diversion” of the chips. The changes are a response to a loophole that allowed Chinese firms to rent AI computing power from data centers in Southeast Asia and elsewhere that run on US hardware not available for export to China. While the loophole has been known to authorities, the revelation of Huang’s affair has drawn intense scrutiny to the practice. His lover Alice Huang, who is not related to the 63-year-old, is a former executive of Megaspeed — a Singapore-based cloud computing firm under US criminal investigation for allegedly helping Chinese companies procure advanced Nvidia AI chips in circumvention of export controls. Investors are watching for signs of whether Kress will slow Huang’s aggressive investment strategy, which saw him commit tens of billions of dollars to AI companies. Huang on Tuesday sounded a note of contrition in his statement, saying “I did not live up to the standards expected of everyone at NVIDIA, and I have made serious mistakes in my personal life.” The post Nvidia says no return for ousted CEO, reports revenue boom appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Tourism Society, University of Ghana to host three-day youth festival
items.description: The Tourism Society of Ghana, in collaboration with the University of Ghana, Legon, is set to host a three-day festival to promote youth participation in domestic tourism and the preservation of Ghanaian culture. The 2026 Youth in Tourism Festival (YOTOFEST) will take place from Thursday, November 19 to Saturday, November 21, at the VIP Car Park of the University of Ghana Sports Stadium in Accra. The festival, which will be held under the theme “My Culture, My Pride – The Role of the Youth in Promoting Domestic Tourism,” seeks to encourage young people to explore Ghana’s tourism attractions, appreciate their cultural heritage and contribute to the growth of the tourism industry. The organisers say the initiative will provide a platform for tourism education, entrepreneurship, cultural expression, entertainment and engagement between young people and industry players. Activities lined up for the three-day event include a Tourism Summit, Campus Tourism Tour, Tourism Fair and Exhibition, Bajoo Night and a Health Walk. The Tourism Summit will bring together students, academics, tourism professionals and other industry stakeholders to discuss opportunities for young people in the sector. Discussions are expected to focus on tourism entrepreneurship, cultural preservation, destination marketing, innovation and career opportunities within the industry. Participants will also have the opportunity to experience aspects of Ghana’s tourism offerings through a Campus Tourism Tour featuring the Visit Ghana double-decker tourism bus. The Tourism Fair and Exhibition will provide a platform for hotels, travel agencies, tour operators, tourism destinations, hospitality businesses and other industry players to showcase their products and services. Bajoo Night will add an entertainment component to the festival, featuring music, cultural performances and youth creativity, while a health walk will promote physical fitness and healthy living. This year’s festival will also coincide with the 20th anniversary of the Tourism Society of Ghana, providing an opportunity to reflect on the organisation’s contribution to tourism education, professional development and industry promotion over the past two decades. The organisers say the festival is intended to strengthen domestic tourism by encouraging Ghanaians, particularly the youth, to explore local destinations and support businesses operating within the tourism value chain. Ghana’s cultural heritage, including traditional festivals, historic castles and forts, palaces, indigenous cuisine, music, dance and crafts, presents opportunities for tourism development and job creation. However, the organisers believe that sustained growth in the sector will depend partly on the willingness of young people to appreciate, preserve and promote these resources. Call for corporate support Ahead of the festival, the Tourism Society of Ghana is calling on corporate organisations, financial institutions, telecommunications companies, airlines, hospitality businesses and development partners to support the initiative. The organisers say corporate participation will offer businesses opportunities to engage young consumers, showcase their products, establish partnerships and contribute to youth development and cultural preservation. Organisations are being invited to participate through various sponsorship and partnership arrangements, including title sponsorship, platinum, gold and silver sponsorships, as well as official, supporting and media partnerships. The organisers also envisage the festival creating opportunities for mentorship, internships, skills development and tourism entrepreneurship beyond the three-day event. They say the partnership with the University of Ghana provides an opportunity to strengthen collaboration between educational institutions, tourism businesses and young people. The organisers are urging corporate Ghana and other stakeholders to support YOTOFEST 2026, describing it as an investment in youth development, cultural preservation and the future of Ghana’s domestic tourism industry.

items.title: Kwara APC Reps candidate unveils people-centred agenda
items.description: …Says serving as AbdulRazaq’s CPS was greatest privilege By Demola Akinyemi, Ilorin ILORIN — The All Progressives Congress (APC) candidate for Ifelodun/Offa/Oyun Federal Constituency in the House of Representatives election, Dr Rafiu Ajakaye, has unveiled a legislative agenda focusing on security, education, youth employment, women’s economic empowerment and rural development. Ajakaye, a former Chief Press Secretary to Kwara State Governor AbdulRahman AbdulRazaq, said his aspiration to represent the constituency was driven by a desire to provide accessible and effective leadership rather than pursue personal ambition. He stated this on Tuesday while speaking on the News Keg programme organised by the Correspondents’ Chapel of the Nigeria Union of Journalists (NUJ) at its secretariat in Ilorin. Presenting his manifesto titled, “Manifesto of Purpose: A Covenant with the People of Ifelodun/Offa/Oyun Federal Constituency”, Ajakaye described his service as the governor’s spokesperson as a major privilege in his professional career. “Serving as the Chief Press Secretary to Governor AbdulRahman AbdulRazaq was one of the greatest privileges of my life,” he said. He described public office as a responsibility that should be directed towards improving people’s lives. Ajakaye cited his involvement in the 2021, 2024 and 2025 teachers’ recruitment exercises under the AbdulRazaq administration as an experience that reinforced his belief in merit-based employment opportunities. According to him, the exercises demonstrated the importance of involving the right people in recruitment processes to ensure fairness and create opportunities for qualified applicants. “Leadership is not about occupying an office. It is about inspiring hope, solving problems, expanding opportunities, and shaping a future in which every citizen can live with dignity,” he said. The candidate, who hails from Alabe community in Ifelodun Local Government Area, said his background, academic training and professional experience had shaped his approach to governance and public service. He said his experience as a journalist, public relations practitioner and public servant, particularly his years as the governor’s spokesperson, had exposed him to policymaking and the importance of transparency, competence and integrity in governance. On security, Ajakaye identified banditry and kidnapping as major concerns affecting rural communities, saying the activities had disrupted livelihoods and economic activities. He pledged to advocate stronger legislative oversight of security agencies, improved welfare and equipment for security personnel, intelligence-led operations and community-based security strategies. He identified insecurity in parts of Ifelodun Local Government Area as a major priority, promising to make it the foremost issue on his legislative agenda if elected. “Security is number one on my legislative agenda. I understand the pains of my people because that is where I come from, If elected, I will champion stronger legislative oversight of security agencies,” he said. On education, the APC candidate said he would advocate reforms to align the country’s education system with technological developments and labour market demands. He identified science, technical, vocational and digital education as areas requiring greater attention. Addressing youth unemployment, Ajakaye promised to support legislation that would promote entrepreneurship, improve access to finance for small businesses, strengthen vocational training and encourage young people to embrace agriculture. On women’s economic empowerment, he said he would pursue policies to support women-owned businesses through affordable financing, cooperative initiatives, improved market access and sustainable income-generating opportunities. He also pledged to promote rural infrastructure, agricultural modernisation, small business development and improved public services, insisting that development should extend to every ward and community in the constituency. The post Kwara APC Reps candidate unveils people-centred agenda appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Matawalle’s support group targets release of 2,000 inmates
items.description: By Musa Ubandawaki, Sokoto SOKOTO — The Tinubu Again Movement (TAM), a political support group associated with the Minister of State for Defence, Bello Matawalle, has announced plans to facilitate the release of 2,000 inmates in Sokoto, Kebbi and Zamfara states through the payment of court-imposed fines and other lawful interventions. The proposed initiative is aimed at assisting indigent inmates whose continued detention is linked to their inability to pay fines and those eligible for release under applicable laws. The group announced the plan on Tuesday during its participation in the presidential campaign rally of President Bola Tinubu in Birnin Kebbi, Kebbi State. Hundreds of its members participated in the rally, wearing branded outfits and carrying banners bearing the images of Tinubu, Vice-President Kashim Shettima and Matawalle. The supporters also marched through major streets of the state capital, expressing support for the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) ahead of the 2027 general elections. Speaking on the proposed intervention, TAM spokesman, Mallam Yusuf Dingyadi, said the initiative was designed to assist deserving inmates who could not secure their release because of financial constraints. He said the movement would identify eligible beneficiaries and work towards settling outstanding fines in accordance with the law. “Our intention is to facilitate the release of 2,000 inmates across Sokoto, Kebbi and Zamfara states by identifying deserving cases and assisting those whose continued detention is linked to their inability to pay relatively small fines. “We believe that imprisonment should not become a permanent barrier to rebuilding one’s life, particularly for individuals who qualify for release under the law but remain in correctional facilities because of their financial circumstances,” Dingyadi said. He added that the intervention was intended to support family reunification and the reintegration of eligible former inmates into society. Dingyadi also disclosed that the movement was planning humanitarian interventions for internally displaced persons (IDPs) and other vulnerable communities across the three states. According to him, the proposed programmes would include the distribution of food, clothing and other essential relief materials, as well as empowerment initiatives. “We are equally concerned about the humanitarian challenges confronting internally displaced persons in Sokoto, Kebbi and Zamfara states. We intend to support them through the provision of foodstuffs, clothing and empowerment opportunities to cushion their hardships and restore their dignity,” he said. On the proposed inmate-release programme, Dingyadi said the group would engage relevant correctional authorities, judicial institutions and other stakeholders to identify eligible beneficiaries and ensure compliance with existing laws. He stressed that the initiative was not intended to interfere with judicial decisions but to support lawful processes for the release of inmates who had met the relevant conditions for discharge. Beyond the humanitarian initiative, the TAM spokesman said the group’s participation in the Kebbi rally reflected its commitment to grassroots mobilisation for Tinubu’s re-election bid in 2027. He said the movement planned to expand its political activities across the North-West through engagements with communities and political stakeholders. If implemented, the proposed intervention could provide relief to affected inmates and their families, while drawing attention to the challenges faced by indigent persons unable to meet court-imposed financial obligations. items.title: Bankrolling attacks in Gaza: How a global bank arms Israel
items.description: As the world eased into the new year in January 2022, a committee at Deutsche Bank headquarters in Frankfurt prepared to discuss if the bank should go ahead with deals which could hurt its reputation. On its agenda for the Jan 12 meeting was EUR 11.4 million advance payment guarantee to German defence manufacturer Renk GmbH, to fund a contract with the Israeli Ministry of Defence that would continue until 2027. Renk was to make gearboxes for its Merkava 4 tanks, with the first of the products to be delivered in September 2024. A document weighing up the deal had been on the tables of Deutsche Bank’s decision makers since Dec 16, 2021. An assistant general counsel for the bank was among those who contributed his views. He thought the deal involved a “plain vanilla trade finance product which does not carry any remarkable RepRisk in itself.” He said the likelihood of the deal becoming public was “very low”. But the risk would be even lower if the financing guarantees could be made via an Israeli bank on Deutsche Bank’s behalf, he said. The gearboxes, he added, were not considered weapons under the German Military Weapons Act, and Renk will secure a license to export them. “I am supportive of the transaction,” he said. The deal went ahead. Merkava 4 against civilians Two years later, in January 2024, six-year-old Palestinian Hind Rajab was on the phone to emergency services, pleading to be rescued. Rajab and six family members were fleeing Israeli attacks in Gaza when the car they were travelling in was shot at. By that point, she was the only one still alive. After hours of negotiation for safe passage, an ambulance crew heading to rescue the preschooler was intercepted. It would be days before the bodies of the first responders, Hind and her family, could be reached. A total of 335 bullet holes were found on the family’s car. The Israeli government initially said none of its forces was present, and later claimed the bullet holes came from crossfire. However, satellite imagery and audio analysis of the incident by Forensic Architecture, a research group at Goldsmiths, University of London, found only the presence of the Israeli Defence Force (IDF) at the scene. In an October 2025 filing to the International Criminal Court, the Hind Rajab Foundation alleged that the tanks were Merkava 4. A tank round was found among the remains of the ambulance crew that had attempted to rescue Rajab. On Aug 19, 2026, more than two years after the incident, the IDF confirmed that its soldiers had opened fire on the car Rajab had been in, as well as at the rescue ambulance. It blamed the shooting on “failures in the co-ordination of the movement of the Palestine Red Crescent Society ambulance,” a claim the PRCS refuted. The IDF said a criminal investigation would be undertaken. This wasn’t the first documented event where Merkava tanks — the main tanks used in Gaza — were used against civilians since January 2022, when the bank’s Reputational Review committee supported the deal. Among the most high-profile cases involving Merkava tanks are the siege on Gaza’s Al Shifa Hospital in November 2023 and the fatal attack on civilians waiting for food aid at the Al Tahliya roundabout, as the famine in Gaza worsened in June 2025. This was about nine months after the stated delivery date of the new Renk gearboxes and a month after the IDF published photos of the Renk gearboxes being prepared for mounting. Sufian Kawareh, 43, had no choice but to go to the relief aid distribution route east of Khan Yunis, in the southern Gaza Strip, to wait among the crowds for trucks loaded with flour. At the “Al-Tahliya” roundabout — where Kawareh and thousands of starving people sat waiting for the trucks to arrive — shells fired from Israeli Merkava tanks struck the area. Kawareh felt “an iron saw cutting through his leg” and soon collapsed. After a week of suffering, doctors amputated his foot to keep him alive. Khaled Walid, 40, who was injured in the Al Tahliya incident, recalled a Merkava 4 tank shooting at the crowd. It was easily distinguishable from other tanks used by the Israeli army, he said. “It had a turret, a cannon, a machine gun and metal structures surrounding its body,” he said in an interview. Palestinian authorities said at least 59 people who had been waiting for aid were killed in the incident. The IDF said a crowd had gathered near a stuck aid truck close to its troops, that the details were under review, and that it “regrets any harm to uninvolved individuals. Nasser Medical Complex, the hospital that treated victims of the Al Tahliya roundabout attack, itself came under shelling from a Merkava tank a couple of months later, on Aug 25, 2025, killing Reuters journalist Husam al-Masri. When rescue workers and journalists rushed to the scene, the same tank returned and shelled the hospital again, according to eyewitness and journalist Osama Hisham, whose tent was opposite the Nasser Medical Complex. IDF officials cited by Israeli media at the time also said the same tank had fired twice. A total of 22 Palestinians , including five journalists, some from Reuters and the Associated Press , rescue workers, and a health worker, were killed. The next day, the IDF said it was targeting a camera used by Hamas, but Reuters confirmed the camera belonged to the news agency. Shown photos of the shells from this incident during an interview, explosives engineer Mohamed Salem, who has experience in explosives disposal in conflict zones, confirmed the attack was the result of 120 mm artillery ammunition designed for the smooth-bore guns of the Merkava tanks. The standard marking “CRTG 120” is visible on the projectile wall. Several of the high-profile incidents involving the Merkava 4 happened before the first batch of supply supported by Deutsche Bank was scheduled to be delivered in September 2024. According to our information, the incidents in Gaza did not affect the Deutsche Bank-Renk deal. The Merkava 4 The Merkava 4 Back Next Tap the rings on the tank to jump to the text. 120-mm cannon Trophy system Roof machine guns In Gaza Illustration by Beatrice Cambarau / IrpiMedia "> Negative press In the December 2021 internal Reputational Risk memo, it was noted that given a rise in Israel-Palestine and Israel-Lebanon tensions across that year, “including cross-border strikes and violent treatment of protestors,” the deal was not without risk. However, declining such a deal might also invite “negative press” for the bank, given the “historic relationship of Germany and Israel”. “If non-participation becomes public, we could face criticism from media/government that we deny necessary support to Israel to allow its self-defense,” the memo reads. “Former Chancellor Angela Merkel just stated during her last visit to Israel in Oct. 2021 that the security of Israel is part of our “reason of state” and Germany is not neutral regarding the question of Israel’s security.” Every Deutsche Bank department consulted in the review said that on balance, the deal should go ahead. As the violence escalated in Gaza, Deutsche Bank remained committed to Renk. On Feb 7, 2024, when Renk went public on the Frankfurt Stock Exchange, Deutsche Bank acted as one of the coordinators of its Initial Public Offering alongside Citigroup, Goldman Sachs and JP Morgan. Court case One of the justifications given by Deutsche Bank to support the Merkava 4 deal in 2022 was that the exports would still need to be approved by the German government. However, for most of 2024, hardly any export licences for Israel were approved in Germany, something that affected Renk and Rolls-Royce, who manufactured the Merkava 4 supply engines, sources familiar with the industry said. They said the supply issues jeopardised the Israeli ground offensive. Israel had ramped up its offensive significantly after the Hamas-led Oct 7, 2023 attack on South Israel that killed 1,200 people, including 815 civilians. In August 2025, the German government suspended the export of weapons to Israel. Around the same time, a regional appeals court in Hesse, Germany was considering a challenge brought by a Palestinian man in Gaza, who sought to halt German export licences for Renk tank transmission parts bound for Israel. He argued that the licences breached Germany’s constitutional duty to protect his right to life. A Frankfurt court had rejected his application in December 2024, finding he had no standing, and in September 2025 the appeals court upheld that ruling. Two months later, the German government lifted its partial military exports suspension to Israel, citing the ceasefire announced the month before. A year on, a UN inquiry found Israel continued committing “genocidal acts with the genocidal intent to destroy, in whole or in part, the Palestinians in Gaza”. Israel rejects this characterisation. More than 1,600 Palestinians — mostly civilians — have been killed in Israeli attacks since the ceasefire. When contacted, Renk declined to comment. Rolls-Royce did not respond to our requests for comment. A bomb made to penetrate forts Renk is not the only defence manufacturer whose products were used by the IDF against civilians, nor the only one supported by Deutsche Bank, posing a question about compliance with the bank’s own human rights policy. “Our principle is not to engage in any business activities where Deutsche Bank has substantiated evidence of material adverse human rights impacts and where it is determined through the bank’s internal processes that such adverse human rights impacts cannot be avoided or appropriately mitigated,” the bank says in its statement on human rights. Another defence manufacturer with ties to Deutsche Bank is the Italian arms manufacturer Leonard S.p.a (partially State-owned). By October 2018, the bank was involved in a multi-million-euro Israel-related deal with Leonardo. The bank had been asked to issue trade-related guarantees to the Italian defence firm, which was described internally as a “platinum client”. Leonardo produced the 76/62 Super Rapid Multi-Feeding Naval Gun Mounts , a weapon that can fire 120 rounds a minute, for Israel’s Sa’ar 6-class corvettes — Israel’s newest and most advanced warships. The IDF has used these warships to shell Gaza from the sea since 2023. The 76/62 Super Rapid Multi-Feeding Naval Gun Mounts were produced and delivered in a deal guaranteed by Deutsche Bank. Leonardo, via a subsidiary, also makes automatic loaders for the Trophy APS system that protects ground vehicles against potential attacks, including the Merkava 4 . Leonardo is currently facing a lawsuit by a Palestinian citizen and several Italian advocacy groups for breaching the Italian Constitution by allegedly supplying weapons to Israel that were used to violate human rights. Leonardo’s CEO last year refuted accusations that his company was complicit in the Gaza conflict. In a response to questions from Barracuda Media, the company acknowledged its relationship with Deutsche Bank. It said it has always operated in strict compliance with national and international regulations governing the export of defense equipment and dual-use goods, as well as in accordance with authorisations granted by the competent authorities. It noted that following the escalation of the Israeli-Palestinian conflict, Italian authorities have suspended the issuance of new licenses for the export of defense equipment to Israel. In 2024, BankTrack and 18 other civil society organisations published a report detailing how commercial banks were financing companies that arm Israel weapons. Deutsche Bank, it found, had extended about EUR4 billion in loans and underwriting to defence manufacturers Boeing, Leonardo, Lockheed Martin, Rolls Royce, RTX Corp and General Dynamics between January 2021 and August 2023, although not all their products were used in Gaza. One of the bombs made by Boeing, with key components provided by a joint venture 25 per cent owned by Leonardo, is the GBU Small Diameter Bomb. The bomb was used by the IDF via its air force to strike homes and urban areas. According to two weapons experts who reviewed photos of the aftermath, it was likely used in the attack on the Al-Mutanabbi School near Khan Younis in July 2024 that claimed the lives of 29 Palestinians. Analysing photos of the aftermath of the attack, explosives engineer Muhammad Salem said bomb fragments seen at the scene certainly came from precision-guided bombs of the “GBU-39” type, or to its fine suspension and control system, based on the serial number printed on the metal. The fragments also revealed the manufacturer code registered to Woodward Inc., one of the suppliers of electromechanical systems and guidance actuators for the Boeing. In addition, the numbers showed the exact manufacturing date of the part on March 31, 2022 (2022-03-31), Salem said. He added that the bomb was designed to penetrate forts. Arms expert Hadavi agrees. In photos of the aftermath, at least one of the GBU Small Diameter Bomb’s four tail-mounted control surfaces, or the “tail wing”, can be seen, he said. Boeing also makes the bigger and stronger GBU-31, which was dropped on displaced people in tents in the al-Mawasi area of Khan Younis on July 13, 2024. That attack left more than 300 injured and killed 91 Palestinians, according to statistics from the Palestinian Ministry of Health at the time. On November 12, 2026, the US-made 250-pound GBU-39/B bomb was used in an IDF airstrike against Nasser Medical Complex , killing at least six people , including a child and prominent surgeon Dr Rizk Abu Shaira, and wounding 52 others . In a statement , the IDF said it was targeting Hamas militants hiding inside the hospital, but Hamas denied this. Since Oct 7, 2023, Israel has killed more than 75,000 people in Palestine and more than 3,000 in South Lebanon. The deaths include hundreds of journalists and aid workers, more than 1,700 healthcare workers and medical personnel and at least 20,000 children. According to a UN inquiry , children were deliberately targeted “using quadcopters, drones, and sniper rifles…to their head and upper body”. BankTrack’s human rights lead Ryan Brightwell said that financial institutions have clear human rights responsibilities. “They need to show how they respect human rights and they’re expected to use their leverage over clients to ensure that they’re not causing or contributing to harms,” he said. If a bank engages with an arms company, “it should be considering divesting or ending the relationship if the client doesn’t change its behaviour,” he added. Boeing did not respond to our questions. Controversial weapons In March 2019, Deutsche Bank expanded its defence policy , which it said “makes clear” it would avoid “entering into, or continuing, any kind of business relationship” with entities that have “clear, direct links” to controversial weapons. Controversial weapons policies “can include landmines, cluster munitions, nuclear weapons or any kind of weapons that are likely to cause indiscriminate harm. And white phosphorus would clearly fall into that bracket,” said Bank Track’s Brightwell. White phosphorus is known for setting buildings on fire and burning flesh to bone. As of June 30, 2026, the bank owns 0.14pc of ICL Group, a white phosphorus supplier, through shares worth US$8.98 million. It also held Israel Chemical Ltd (ICL) bonds as late as August 2019, months after its policy expansion. Two ICL subsidiaries, ICL Performance Products and ICL-IP America , have supplied white phosphorus to a US Army plant in Arkansas that fills artillery shells, on multiple occasions since 2008, according to published Army contracts . The Washington Post and Amnesty International have reported that shells from that plant were exported to Israel. Since 2023, the IDF has deployed projectile artillery made with white phosphorus in Gaza and South Lebanon more than a dozen times, HRW reported . Deutsche Bank internal correspondence suggests how the bank could be employing a loophole in its own policy, by differentiating a parent company and wholly-owned subsidiaries, when defining “direct links” to companies involved in the production and supply of controversial weapons. In December 2019, a Deutsche Bank reputational risk officer in London told colleagues that transactions involving multinational giant Bayer Group did not have to be flagged for controversial weapons. Instead, only transactions involving Monsanto Co, a fully-owned Bayer subsidiary, needed to be flagged. ICL provides phosphate to Monsanto for the production of white phosphorus, later used to make munitions, according to arms trade watchdog Corruption Tracker . ICL, the Bayer Group, the IDF and Deutsche Bank did not respond to our questions on white phosphorus. A lucrative deal After spending about two decades researching global arms procurement, Andrew Feinstein believes that when it comes to defence deals, financial institutions are primarily motivated by only two things: profit and reputation. “They honestly don’t care a damn about how many people might get killed, violations of international humanitarian law, war crimes […] unless it’s going to have an impact on their reputation,” said Feinstein, who is executive director of Shadow World Investigations, a UK-based non-profit investigating corruption in arms trade. At the operational level, he said, this could see bank officers clashing with often “junior” compliance officers, in order to secure their own annual bonuses. “If you’re generating a certain income [for the company], that is reflected in your annual bonus. So you’re talking about people who are making decisions that are going to personally determine whether they personally make tens of thousands of euros or millions of euros at the end of that financial year,” he said in an interview . In January 2021, Deutsche Bank mulled over a potential lucrative deal with Israeli defence maker Israel Aerospace Industries (IAI), even though the Israeli defence maker was off-boarded because it produced controversial weapons. IAI produced the Harpy in the 1980s, a drone which flies over battlefields searching for enemy radar signals before autonomously attacking the targets. The Harpy was one of the Lethal Autonomous Weapons Systems (LAWS) flagged by the bank’s internal intelligence unit in April 2019, when the Industry Reputation Risk team considered developing a LAWS policy ahead of the bank’s AGM that year. In December 2019, an internal policy was put in place to exclude “human out of the loop” LAWS, the bank said. But in 2021, a senior corporate relationship manager for Central Europe and Israel pushed for IAI to get a second chance. One of the reasons: EUR1.5 million in annual revenue. At first, he took the case to two of the bank’s reputation and risk specialists, but both declined due to IAI’s exposure to controversial weapons. Undeterred, he sought senior management support. “We are currently working on a potential US$150 million AR business opportunity with the US$4.1 billion major defence manufacturer Israel Aerospace Industries Ltd. (IAI) as seller and Government of India / Agencies as obligors. The annual revenue potential of this transaction is EUR 1.5mn and additional AR business opportunities could arise later on,” he wrote to a head of trade finance. “We are reaching out to you to get your view as this is a sizable transaction and a sensible reputation risk topic, which would require senior management support in the reputation risk committees,” he said. He said the CEO of IAI had given assurances that the company was not involved in making controversial weapons and would not be doing so in the future. “We need to appeal the decision to a Regional Reputational Risk Committee and then to the Global Reputational Risk Committee,” he wrote to yet another trade finance specialist. But following what appeared to be offline discussions, the trade finance specialist emailed back: “We should pass this one given the public allegations and the uncertainty of the outcome of the BIU report.” “Cc the rep risk team,” he concluded. “Thanks and good luck.” In a response to reporters’ questions, Deutsche Bank did not comment on IAI. IAI did not respond to requests for comment. The IDF declined to comment. Header illustration by Studio Yadi Photos from Gaza by Mohamed Abu Shahma/Daraj The Inside Deutsche Bank investigation was coordinated by Barracuda Media in South Africa, with technical support from the Data and Research Center (DARC) in Germany.

items.title: Audit européen des produits d’origine animale tunisiens destinés à l’exportation
items.description: Une mission d’audit de la Commission européenne a débuté le 16 novembre 2026 en Tunisie afin d’évaluer l’efficacité du système local de contrôle des résidus de médicaments vétérinaires, de pesticides et de contaminants présents chez les animaux et dans les produits d’origine animale destinés à l’exportation vers l’Union européenne (UE). (Photo : Les experts européens ont visité, le 17 novembre, le Laboratoire central d'analyses et d'essais, dans le cadre d'un audit des laboratoires dédiés aux métaux lourds et aux résidus de pesticides, accrédités selon la norme internationale ISO 17025.) La mission, menée par la Direction générale de la santé et de la sécurité alimentaire (DG Santé) de la Commission européenne, en collaboration avec les services vétérinaires du ministère tunisien de l’Agriculture, des Ressources hydrauliques et de la Pêche, se poursuivra jusqu’au 20 novembre. Selon l’agence Tap, les vérifications porteront notamment sur deux filières de production orientées vers le marché européen : l’aquaculture et la production de boyaux naturels salés, utilisés principalement dans l’industrie de la charcuterie. Les experts européens examineront le cadre législatif et réglementaire tunisien, les programmes officiels de surveillance sanitaire, les procédures d'échantillonnage et d'analyse en laboratoire, ainsi que les mécanismes de gestion des non-conformités et de formation du personnel. Des visites dans des entreprises, des laboratoires et auprès des services vétérinaires régionaux sont également prévues. Quelques jours après le début de la mission, la Tunisie a publié, le 10 novembre au Journal officiel, deux nouveaux arrêtés ministériels réglementant l’utilisation des médicaments antimicrobiens à usage vétérinaire ainsi que le programme national de contrôle des substances pharmacologiquement actives chez les animaux aquatiques destinés à la production alimentaire. Ces mesures prévoient, entre autres, le renforcement de la traçabilité des traitements médicamenteux et de la surveillance des résidus, dans le but notamment de lutter contre la résistance aux antimicrobiens. La mission s’inscrit dans le cadre de la coopération sanitaire et commerciale entre Tunis et Bruxelles, avec pour objectif de renforcer la fiabilité du système tunisien de contrôle vétérinaire, de protéger la santé des consommateurs et de consolider l’accès des produits agroalimentaires du pays nord-africain au marché communautaire. I. B. L’article Audit européen des produits d’origine animale tunisiens destinés à l’exportation est apparu en premier sur Kapitalis .

items.title: Immigration vows to fix gaps in Visa & Residency Reforms
items.description: .As Army pledges stronger partnership on border security By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA: The Nigeria Immigration Service NIS on Tuesday undertook a stakeholders’ assessment of its Visa and Residency Reforms, one year after the scheme was rolled out, promising to confront all the weak points. Comptroller General of the NIS, Kemi Nandap, made the pledge in Abuja, while declaring open a one-day stakeholders’ sensitization workshop on the Nigeria Visa and Residency Reforms. At the event, the Nigerian Army also pledged a stronger partnership with the Service in securing the country’s borders, especially in areas where a large portion of the frontier remains porous. The Chief of Civil-Military Affairs (Army), Major General Musa Etsu-Ndagi, who represented the Chief of Army Staff COAS, said: “Nigeria has a land border of 4,047km and there is a large portion of it that remains porous. The Nigerian Army will continue to support the NIS in manning the borders especially in those areas”. On the reforms, the CGIS who was represented by the Deputy Comptroller General DCG in charge of Visa and Residency, Dr Franca Usiwoma Nwanneka, said; “As we assess the implementation of the reforms over the last one year, we have reasons to appreciate the progress made so far. However, we must also be ready to identify the areas where we have not done well and take the necessary steps to address them”. The workshop was held under the theme: “Assessing the Implementation of the Nigeria Visa and Residency Reforms: Stakeholders’ Engagement and Strategies for Improved Service Delivery.” Nandap said the purpose of the meeting was to look at the progress made since the introduction of the reforms, discuss the challenges encountered and identify areas where improvements are needed.” She acknowledged that users may have run into difficulties since the introduction of these reforms. “These may include payment difficulties, technical issues and other concerns relating to the use of the portal. I want to assure you that the Service is willing to listen to your concerns and consider useful recommendations that will help us improve our operations,” she said. According to her, the reforms were introduced “to address some of the challenges associated with the old manual processes, reduce delays, improve transparency, strengthen national security and make our immigration services more accessible to the public.” Nandap listed the electronic visa (e-Visa) among the major gains, noting that it became operational on 1st May, 2025, and replaced the traditional Visa-on-Arrival arrangement. “Applicants can now receive decisions on their visa applications within 48 hours, subject to meeting the necessary requirements and security checks,” she said. She added that the e-Visa had “improved transparency, reduced unnecessary human interference and strengthened our ability to monitor visa applications and approvals.” The Comptroller General also cited the creation of the F9A and F9B visa categories for adult and minor Nigerians returning with foreign passports respectively, which she said had “helped to address the needs of Nigerians in the diaspora who find themselves in this situation.” On work permits, Nandap said the Electronic Temporary Work Permit (e-TWP) became operational on 1st August, 2025, replacing manual procedures that “sometimes resulted in delays.” According to her, biometric capturing machines had improved the identification and verification of applicants, while insurance requirements were introduced to improve the management of foreign nationals undertaking temporary work in Nigeria. The e-TWP, she explained, is also linked to the Service’s border management system through the Landing and Exit Card facility, which “will assist in monitoring the movement of foreign nationals and ensuring that they comply with the conditions of their stay in Nigeria.” The third pillar of the reforms, the electronic Comprehensive Expatriate Residence Permit and Automated Card (e-CERPAC), also took effect on 1st August, 2025. Nandap said the system had improved the handling of residence permit applications, renewals and status regularisation, and led to the introduction of the Investors Residence Permit in support of the Federal Government’s drive to attract investment. She said the e-CERPAC’s integration with the border management system “will make it easier to verify the residence status of expatriates at our entry and exit points.” The immigration boss stressed that the Service could not succeed alone, and called for the support of “relevant Ministries, Departments and Agencies, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Nigerian Missions abroad, security agencies, the private sector, international organisations and employers of expatriates.” Urging participants to contribute actively, Nandap said: “Our goal is to have an immigration system that provides efficient services, protects the security of our country and supports the economic development of Nigeria.” The post Immigration vows to fix gaps in Visa & Residency Reforms appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: FMCGs seek NAFDAC automation to cut registration delays, fake licences
items.description: By Cynthia Alo Fast-Moving Consumer Goods, FMCG, manufacturers and small businesses have urged the National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control, NAFDAC, to automate most of its paper processes involving product registration and licence renewal to reduce delays and curb circulation of counterfeit products and fake registration numbers. They said prolonged approvals were forcing some manufacturers to rely on intermediaries, exposing them to exploitation, including the use of fake NAFDAC registration numbers. The call was made recently at the 2026 FMCG Festival in Lagos. Speaking on behalf of manufacturers, Project Director of the FMCG Festival, Flora Mbeledeogu, said renewal of NAFDAC licences remained a major challenge, and that NAFDAC needed more hands and automation to make registration and renewal faster and more seamless. Mbeledeogu said: “We need NAFDAC to employ more hands and automate our systems so that when a consumer brand wants to renew its NAFDAC certificate or licence, they can do so without having to raise an arm and a leg. It has to just be a seamless process, just like it is in other countries in Africa where you just need to upload the required documents on the portal; within 24 hours, receive notification for factory inspection; officials inspect and take samples; analysis is done;by 48 hours, the product registration number is issued. We need to get to that point.” She warned that delays could expose smaller manufacturers to exploitation by intermediaries who claim to facilitate registration and renewal processes. She urged the agency to address the bottlenecks before the next edition of the festival. Responding to the concerns, Director, NAFDAC, North-West Zone, Dadi Mullah, said the agency’s processes were designed to ensure products met required health and safety standards. He disclosed that food product registration could take up to 120 working days, covering facility inspection, laboratory testing, regulatory assessment and final approval. Mullah said one challenge was that some small businesses wanted to produce from their domestic kitchens without meeting the facility requirements prescribed for commercial production. He said NAFDAC could not allow such businesses to supply the wider market without complying with Good Manufacturing Practices, GMP. He said: “The only thing I know that many of you will complain about is our facility requirement. We insist that unless the facility meets minimum good manufacturing practices requirements, we will not allow you to produce.Your kitchen cannot produce the kind of products for the international market.” Speaking on delays in registration and renewal processing, he said NAFDAC’s laboratories handled a large volume of applications, making it difficult for applicants to expect immediate results. He attributed part of the delays in Lagos to inadequate personnel at the agency’s food registration office. He disclosed that NAFDAC had previously recorded more than 8,400 pending applications partly to having only one Local Office Director (LOD) handling applications at the office adding, “There was only one LOD in the food registration office, and until that person processes all those products, it sits in Lagos pipeline, moving slower.” He said the agency had deployed additional LODs across its zonal offices to reduce the backlog. He expressed optimism that the additional personnel would accelerate the process in the coming months, while urging manufacturers to continue providing feedback on delays and other challenges. He added that to encourage registration of products , NAFDAC had discounted registration fees for micro, small and medium enterprises, MSMEs, since 2020. According to him, no product registration fee exceeds N100,000, while some micro businesses pay between N40,000 and N60,000. He said laboratory analysis could cost about N500,000, with the agency bearing part of the cost. Mullah maintained that manufacturers did not need agents or intermediaries to obtain registration, advising businesses experiencing difficulties with the online process to approach the agency’s support desk for assistance at no cost. He warned that anyone caught dealing in counterfeit products would face the law, saying offenders could be sentenced to seven years in prison. ” For now, anyone that is just dabbling into that, wherever, whenever we catch such a person, we will make sure that the law deals with you.” He said consumers and traders could use NAFDAC’s online verification platform at registration.nafdac.gov.ng to confirm whether a product’s registration number was genuine. He explained that the platform provides information such as the product name, packaging details, registration number and expiry date, enabling consumers to identify fake products. He advised consumers to examine product labels, storage conditions and registration numbers before purchasing or consuming regulated products. He also asked them to report suspected counterfeit products through the agency’s website, email and social media platforms, rather than merely complain about their circulation in the market. The NAFDAC official further called for stronger collaboration with traders and distributors to identify and remove unregistered and counterfeit products from markets. Supporting the call, President, Okearin Traders Association, Paulinus Ugwu , said traders had established a task force in the market to identify and remove counterfeit products. Ugwu called for closer collaboration between traders and NAFDAC, noting that regulators could not know everything happening in markets without the cooperation of those operating there. He said traders were also interested in promoting locally manufactured products, particularly those produced by small businesses, and called on manufacturers to bring their product samples for consideration by distributors. In his keynote address, the Chief Operating Officer of Berger Paints Nigeria Plc, Kayode Momoh, urged manufacturers to strengthen supply chains, local sourcing, product quality and innovation to remain competitive. Momoh said innovation must go beyond developing new ideas to ensuring that products could be produced, delivered and sustained consistently in the market. He also called for a stable and predictable regulatory environment to give manufacturers confidence to invest for the long term. The post FMCGs seek NAFDAC automation to cut registration delays, fake licences appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Balla Gaye 2 tient son open press à Ziguinchor : la Casamance comme bouclier mystique ?
items.description: Pour la première fois de sa carrière, Balla Gaye 2 (Balla Gaye) délocalise son open press en Casamance, précisément à Ziguinchor, à quelques jours de son combat contre Ada Fass (Fass-Benno), prévu le 29 novembre 2026. Un retour aux sources qui alimente les supputations. Certains y voient une stratégie destinée à se prémunir contre les éventuelles pratiques mystiques de son jeune adversaire. Hier, mardi 17 novembre, Balla Gaye 2 était au stade Aline Sitoé Diatta de Ziguinchor pour y tenir son open press. Depuis le début de sa carrière, en 2005, le « Lion de Guédiawaye » n’avait jamais organisé un tel rendez-vous en Casamance, la terre de ses parents, tous originaires de cette région verdoyante. Un choix qui n’est certainement pas anodin. Depuis le décès de son père, Double Less, survenu le 5 septembre 2021, Balla Gaye 2 s’était fait rare en Casamance. Il ne s’y rendait plus pour s’y ressourcer mystiquement. Son père y séjournait pendant plusieurs semaines pour rassembler l’arsenal mystique destiné à ses héritiers. Pourtant, après ses saisons fructueuses ou ses grandes victoires, il sillonnait les profondeurs de la Casamance naturelle pour organiser la « Caravane de la paix ». C’était sa manière de contribuer à l’effort de ses parents et de leur témoigner sa reconnaissance pour leur rôle supposé dans ses succès. Mais l’aîné de Sa Thiès avait fini par couper le « cordon ombilical » avec ses parents du Sud. A lire aussi : Quel Balla Gaye 2 face à Ada Fass le 29 novembre ? Sur le plan mystique, il avait fait appel à d’autres personnes pour assurer sa protection. Seulement, face à ses performances en baisse et à la facilité avec laquelle certains adversaires parvenaient à le mettre en difficulté, au point que certaines de ses défaites semblaient inexplicables aux yeux de ses supporters, le lutteur a visiblement décidé de renouer avec ses racines et de lancer un appel à la Casamance. Le premier acte posé dans ce sens a été d’associer la tradition casamançaise à son récent rendez-vous avec la presse. Ce jour-là, le leader de l’école Balla Gaye s’était habillé aux couleurs de la tradition casamançaise et avait esquissé des pas de danse au rythme des sonorités mandingues et diolas, comme pour signifier à ses parents qu’il était de retour aux sources. C’est également à cette occasion qu’il avait lancé un appel solennel à Albourakh Events pour l’aider à organiser son prochain open press en Casamance. Le promoteur et ses collaborateurs lui ont réservé une suite favorable. Mais que cache cette volonté affichée de renouer avec la Casamance ? Selon plusieurs observateurs, Balla Gaye 2 redouterait la puissance mystique d’Ada Fass. Il ne voudrait surtout pas être atteint et perdre facilement son duel. Pour preuve, interpellé sur la dernière victoire de son adversaire face à Eumeu Sène, le 19 avril 2025, Balla Gaye 2 avait répondu en ces termes : « Tout le monde sait qu’Eumeu Sène est un grand champion, mais ce jour-là, il n’y a pas eu de combat. » Ce retour aux sources permettra-t-il à Balla Gaye 2 de tirer son épingle du jeu, le dimanche 29 novembre ? Rien n’est moins sûr. Une chose est toutefois certaine : le lutteur a également renoué le fil de ses relations avec certains foyers religieux, sollicités pour prier en faveur de sa victoire. Abdoulaye DEMBÉLÉ

items.title: Abia making steady progress under my watch — Otti
items.description: Pledges support for emerging talents to attain global recognition By Steve Oko UMUAHIA — Abia State Governor, Alex Otti, has said the state is making steady progress, expressing optimism about its development prospects under his administration. Otti spoke at the grand finale of the 13th edition of the Vision Africa Icons Talent Show 2026 in Umuahia, where he highlighted his administration’s efforts to reposition the state’s economy and promote development across various sectors. The governor, who was represented by his Chief of Staff, Pastor Caleb Ajagba, also pledged government support for the discovery, development and international promotion of indigenous talents. He said the administration was committed to creating opportunities for gifted young people to develop their abilities and gain recognition beyond Nigeria. Reflecting on the state’s development journey, Otti said his administration had prioritised efforts to harness Abia’s economic and human resources. “Before Otti came on board, Abia was lying fallow and prostrate. Nothing good was being said of Abia State. Today, Abia is being celebrated as a place of excellence,” he said. The governor said purposeful leadership and collaboration were important in unlocking the state’s human and creative potential. He assured participants in the talent show that the government would support successful contestants in pursuing opportunities for international recognition. Otti also disclosed that the state government would partner with Vision Africa International to advance the initiative. “Everybody that emerges here today is going global. His Excellency is going to make sure that global stardom is achieved,” he said. He described the talent show as consistent with his administration’s commitment to identifying, nurturing and promoting the abilities of young people. Earlier, the Chairman of the occasion, Noah Dallaji, represented by Theo Ubani, said Africa’s human talent remained one of the continent’s major competitive advantages. “I tell people that Africa has talent to offer. We might not offer the best in technology, but what we can offer is talent,” he said. In his welcome address, the founder and President of Vision Africa International, Archbishop Sunday Onuoha, called on political leaders to create conditions that would enable disadvantaged citizens to benefit from peace and development. Onuoha, who is also Co-Chairman of the Interfaith Dialogue Forum for Peace, said Nigeria’s diversity should promote unity rather than division. He urged Nigerians to work together across their differences to build a peaceful and prosperous country. The 13th edition of the Vision Africa Icons Talent Show was held under the theme, “The Sound of Peace: Breaking Barriers, Building Bridges.” The post Abia making steady progress under my watch — Otti appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Itsekiri youths suspend campaign rally boycott after governor’s intervention
items.description: Itsekiri apex youth bodies, Ugbarajo Itsekiri Youths, UIY, and Itsekiri National Youth Council, INYC, have reiterated their opposition to the inclusion of the Ijaw in the Warri South ward delineation. They expressed surprise at the Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC’s, decision to upload wards with names that have no historical, geographical or traditional relationship with Warri South, saying the move could trigger serious crises. They, however, decided to temporarily suspend mass action against all forms of political activities in Warri Kingdom following the intervention of Governor Sheriff Oborevwori. The INYC President, Appearance Efejuku, and UIY President, Joseph Okotie, made this known in a statement. The statement read: “Sequel to the memorandum of threat issued to the general public over the readiness of the Itsekiri apex youth bodies, UIY and INYC, to prevent the hosting of all forms of campaign rallies in any part of Warri Kingdom until all issues associated with the illegal creation of wards for the Ijaws are addressed satisfactorily, the Governor of Delta State, Right Honorable Elder Francis O. Oborevwori, invited us, leaders and other stakeholders, for a closed-door meeting, wherein he requested to know why the issuers of the threats took such a position. According to him, as of the last time he checked, the entire Itsekiri nation endorsed him and Mr. President. Thus, if this issue raised in the memo is not addressed, it could be misconstrued as a change in the position of the Itsekiri nation against the APC as a political party. “In response, the leadership of the two youth bodies was very categorical in their vehement opposition to any inclusion of Ijaws by any consideration into Warri South ward delineation. “As this would amount to disrespecting the directive of the President (His Excellency Bola Ahmed Tinubu), who asked the Itsekiris and the Urhobos of Warri South to go and meet, sort out the issues, and get back to him. They also said that the President further stated that if the parties involved in these delineation issues were not satisfied, he would have no other option than to take the Supreme Court judgment back to the Supreme Court for proper interpretation. “They were therefore surprised to wake up one day and be told, in flagrant disregard of this directive of the President, that INEC had uploaded wards with names that have no historical, geographical or traditional relationship with Warri South. “This, according to the bodies, is a recipe for serious crises if INEC is not made to retrace its steps. “Thereafter, the Governor appealed to the leadership of the youth bodies to sheath their swords so he could take this issue back to the President for better clarification. “Additionally, it was stated that the only ward structure that was operational before now was the 12-ward structure, and it is what will be used to conduct the 2027 general election. “Consequent upon all that was mentioned, the leadership of UIY and INYC met and hereby resolved to temporarily suspend all forms of intended mass action and mobilisation towards stopping all Itsekiris from attending this rally. We therefore call on all members and critical stakeholders of our organisations to be on internal vigilance to monitor the activities of all political parties in the Kingdom to ensure that these ward delineations are not weaponised as a tool to undermine the Itsekiri people in their homeland of the Warri Federal Constituency. “All these positions were corroborated by the Urhobos of Warri South who were in attendance at the meeting.” The post Itsekiri youths suspend campaign rally boycott after governor’s intervention appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Parliament demands independent probe into Manso Keniago deaths
items.description: Parliament’s Human Rights Committee has called for an independent, impartial and transparent investigation into the deadly confrontation between personnel of the National Anti-Illegal Mining Operations Secretariat (NAIMOS) and residents of Manso Keniago in the Ashanti Region. The incident, which occurred on November 11, 2026, in the Amansie South District, reportedly resulted in deaths and injuries, triggering concerns over the conduct of the anti-illegal mining operation. In a press statement issued on November 17, the Committee, chaired by Ernest Yaw Anim, said it was particularly concerned about conflicting accounts surrounding the incident, including the reported use of firearms, the number of casualties and allegations of assault against traditional authorities and other community members. It said the circumstances leading to the confrontation must be thoroughly investigated to establish the facts and determine whether the conduct of the personnel involved complied with the law and applicable standards governing the use of force by law enforcement officials. The Committee further called for anyone found to have acted unlawfully to be held accountable, regardless of their official position or status, insisting that no individual should be shielded from accountability because they acted under official authority. It also urged the authorities to preserve evidence, including firearms, ammunition records, operational orders, medical and post-mortem reports, photographs and video recordings, while ensuring that witnesses and affected families are protected from intimidation or reprisals. The Committee said it would engage the Ministry of Lands and Natural Resources, NAIMOS, the Ghana Police Service and the Commission on Human Rights and Administrative Justice (CHRAJ) as part of its oversight responsibilities. It stressed that although the government has a responsibility to fight illegal mining and protect the country’s natural resources, such operations must respect the Constitution, human dignity and the right to life. “The fight against illegal mining must be pursued with determination, but never at the expense of the rule of law, human dignity and the sanctity of human life,” the statement said. The Committee extended condolences to the bereaved families and wished injured persons a speedy recovery.

items.title: Knights and Ladies of Marshall celebrate 100 years of Catholic service and charity
items.description: The Noble Order of the Knights and Ladies of Marshall is marking its 100th anniversary with a series of activities celebrating a century of commitment to the Catholic Church, charity and service to society. The Order, which was established in Ghana on November 18, 1926, has since expanded beyond the country and supported religious, educational and community development initiatives. Speaking on JoyNews’ AM Show on Tuesday, November 17, 2026, Past Supreme Knight, Sir Knight Brother Dr Peter Acquah, and Substantive Past Supreme Knight, Sir Knight Brother Anthony Kemavor, reflected on the organisation’s history and its contribution to the Church and society. Mr Kemavor described the Knights of Marshall as “a group of Catholic men who are dedicated to the Catholic Church primarily, and of course their nations”. He said the organisation had expanded from Ghana to Togo, Benin, Côte d’Ivoire, London, Sierra Leone and Liberia, with members supporting the Church and wider society through acts of charity. According to him, members provide support to priests, seminaries and other Church institutions, while also promoting the teachings contained in papal encyclicals. Dr Acquah described the Order’s 100-year journey as “very productive, successful, spiritually rewarding”. He said its work had extended beyond the Catholic community, including outreach to young people through its junior councils. He also highlighted the contribution of the organisation’s founding fathers to education, particularly their advocacy around the establishment of St Augustine’s College between 1926 and 1936. Dr Acquah, an environmentalist, also used the interview to raise concerns about illegal mining, describing it as a national challenge that required urgent attention. “It is an issue which we must address as a country, as a matter of urgency,” he said. Mr Kemavor said preparations for the centenary celebrations began after the Order’s 90th anniversary. He disclosed that the organisation, through Marshallans Relief and Development Services, had invested approximately GH¢5.7 million in charitable activities. The figure excludes projects undertaken directly by local councils and courts, he added. As part of the centenary legacy, the Order will present a kindergarten project to the Diocese of Sekondi-Takoradi through the Bishop. The celebrations begin on Wednesday, November 18, with a candlelight procession to St Paul’s Cathedral, followed by a Mass in honour of the Order’s 13 founding fathers. The programme will also include a main anniversary ceremony expected to be attended by the Chief Justice and the Apostolic Nuncio. A banquet and awards night are scheduled for Saturday, November 21, while a thanksgiving Mass will be held on Sunday, November 22, 2026. In his concluding remarks, Dr Acquah reaffirmed the Order’s commitment to “charity, fraternity, and service”. “Charity is love, and God is love,” he said.

items.title: Les missiles balistiques bon marché mettent à mal la doctrine militaire occidentale
items.description: Les avancées technologiques, ayant rendu les missiles balistiques moins onéreux et plus précis, ont permis à l’Iran et aux Houthis de frapper leurs adversaires à travers tout le Moyen-Orient. Le développement et la diffusion de ces armes -autrefois l’apanage exclusif des grandes puissances nucléaires- imposent une refonte de la doctrine militaire sur laquelle repose la pensée stratégique à l’échelle mondiale. (Ph. Les capacités de l’Iran ont été renforcées grâce à des avancées dans la technologie des missiles balistiques.) Imed Bahri Dans le Wall Street Journal , Yaroslav Trofimov affirme que la prolifération de missiles balistiques à moindre coût remet en cause des décennies de doctrine militaire. Alors que les stocks d’intercepteurs de l’armée américaine s’amenuisent, l’Iran et les Houthis ont mis en lumière la vulnérabilité croissante des bases militaires américaines. À l’instar de la révolution des drones observée en Ukraine, cette mutation entraîne des répercussions stratégiques planétaires, notamment pour le dispositif militaire américain en Europe et en Asie où les actifs militaires et les infrastructures critiques sont désormais davantage exposés. L’Iran a tenu | La fin de l’ère américaine Redéfinition du concept de champ de bataille en profondeur Grâce aux progrès réalisés dans le domaine des missiles balistiques, «même des acteurs non étatiques sont désormais capables d’opérer à longue distance, redéfinissant ainsi le concept de champ de bataille en profondeur» , explique Martin Sampson, général de l’armée de l’air britannique à la retraite qui dirige actuellement le bureau Moyen-Orient de l’Institut international d’études stratégiques (IISS) à Londres. Il ajoute que les systèmes de défense n’ont pas encore suivi cette évolution : «Tout ce qui était autrefois considéré comme à l’abri est désormais devenu une cible». Cette année, l’Iran est parvenu à infliger des dommages importants à des bases militaires américaines, contraignant les États-Unis à évacuer des installations majeures dans le golfe Persique. À Bahreïn, les complexes militaires américains situés le long de la corniche de Manama présentent des carcasses calcinées de radars et d’installations de communication détruits. Parallèlement, au Yémen, les Houthis multiplient les attaques contre les aéroports et les infrastructures énergétiques saoudiennes, accentuant ainsi la pression économique sur le voisin le plus riche du Yémen. Les États-Unis et leurs alliés dans la région commencent à faire face à une pénurie de missiles intercepteurs destinés aux systèmes Patriot et Thaad qui constituent les principaux dispositifs de défense contre les missiles balistiques. Plus largement, cette pénurie mondiale a laissé l’Ukraine sans protection face aux salves de missiles russes visant le réseau électrique, les ponts et des installations industrielles vitales. Selon le WSJ , cette pénurie a de graves répercussions sur le mode opératoire de l’armée américaine. Depuis la Seconde Guerre mondiale, Washington s’appuie sur un réseau de bases réparties à travers le monde pour protéger ses alliés et contenir les puissances rivales. Un haut responsable occidental de la défense a fait remarquer que les pays capables d’assurer leur propre défense antimissile balistique deviendraient des sites privilégiés pour les installations militaires américaines dans les années à venir. Un phénomène similaire s’est déjà produit au Moyen-Orient où les opérations militaires américaines se concentrent de plus en plus en Israël, pays qui fabrique et exploite ses propres systèmes de défense antimissile. Le journal américain souligne que les nations occidentales se retrouvent, d’une certaine manière, confrontées à un dilemme historique. Autrefois, les missiles balistiques étaient extrêmement coûteux et imprécis, la doctrine militaire, au milieu et à la fin du XX e siècle, les considérait essentiellement comme des vecteurs destinés à transporter des armes nucléaires. Une technologie qui se diffuse à travers le monde Fabian Hinz, expert en missiles au sein de l’organisation Conflict Armament Research, a déclaré: «Pendant longtemps, ces systèmes étaient si imprécis qu’ils présentaient peu d’intérêt dans le cadre d’un conflit conventionnel, surtout à longue portée. Or, ces dernières décennies, nous avons assisté au développement de missiles balistiques beaucoup plus précis, une technologie initialement maîtrisée par quelques acteurs avancés mais qui se diffuse désormais à travers le monde. La doctrine militaire occidentale a longtemps reposé sur l’obtention rapide d’une supériorité voire d’une suprématie aérienne mais aujourd’hui, même si vos adversaires ne disposent pas de capacités aériennes sophistiquées, ils restent en mesure de frapper vos sites avec des missiles. Il s’agit là d’une différence fondamentale par rapport au mode de guerre occidental tel que nous l’avons connu ces dernières décennies» . Guerre d’Iran | Vers une reconfiguration de l'ordre mondial Le nucléaire a conduit à considérer le développement de défenses antimissiles balistiques comme un facteur de déstabilisation de l’équilibre nucléaire entre les États-Unis et l’Union soviétique, ce développement a d’ailleurs été encadré par des traités internationaux. Par ailleurs, le traité sur les forces nucléaires à portée intermédiaire, conclu entre Moscou et Washington et resté en vigueur jusqu’en 2019, a incité les pays européens à s’abstenir de développer leurs propres capacités en matière de missiles balistiques basés au sol. Dans le contexte des guerres qui font rage en Ukraine et au Moyen-Orient, les missiles intercepteurs balistiques se font rares, ils comptent parmi les équipements militaires les plus coûteux et les plus sophistiqués et ne peuvent être produits que par un nombre restreint d’entreprises occidentales. Lockheed Martin, l’un des principaux fabricants de missiles balistiques, se trouve désormais dans l’incapacité de répondre à la demande mondiale croissante. Les commandes de missiles Patriot PAC-3 et d’intercepteurs Thaad ne pourront être honorées avant les années 2030. L’an prochain, le consortium franco-italien SAMP/T prévoit de lancer la production de la nouvelle génération de missiles Aster conçus pour contrer les menaces balistiques. Par ailleurs, l’Allemagne déploie actuellement le système antimissile balistique israélien Arrow 3. Parallèlement, comme l’ont démontré les Houthis, les obstacles à l’acquisition d’une capacité de missiles balistiques s’amenuisent rapidement. Selon Fabian Hoffmann, expert en missiles à l’Institut norvégien d’études de défense, l’avantage penchera, dans un avenir proche, en faveur de celui qui attaque. L’article Les missiles balistiques bon marché mettent à mal la doctrine militaire occidentale est apparu en premier sur Kapitalis .
